note: Wild Florida (John, 2026-11-16): Uncle Dan's field school, a game that teaches a 10-to-teen reader to name the major animals of Florida. One entry per animal: 'tell' is the tell-tale shown on screen and used as a clue (it never names the animal); 'dan' is Uncle Dan's spoken line (the book narrator's voice, John's call); 'like' lists look-alikes for the side-by-side rounds; 'regions' and 'type' drive the filters; 'starter' marks the free dozen; 'book' is a tie to the novel taken from fish.json / wildlife.json; 'art' points at the plate; 'draw' is what the artist was asked for; 'more' lists close-up plates (with a caption) for tell-tales that one picture cannot show. Kept simple on purpose: the major animals, not every sub-species. No sizes, seasons or legal rules are stated.
title: Wild Florida
subtitle: Uncle Dan’s field school
intro: I’m Dan. Around here, folks just call me Uncle Dan. You can’t guide a boat full of people if you can’t tell them what just swam past, flew over, slid off the bank or crawled up your leg. So we’re going to learn Florida’s animals the way I learned them: look for the one thing that gives each of them away. Start with a dozen. I’ll be right here.

animals.name: Snook
animals.tell: Long and silver, lower jaw sticking out, one black stripe from gill to tail.
animals.dan: Snook. See that one black stripe down the side, like somebody drew it with a marker? Nothing else wears it. My nephew Matt caught a monster at South Point.
animals.book: Matt’s big snook at South Point, Chapter 6.

animals.name: Tarpon
animals.tell: Huge silver scales, a mouth that scoops upward, one long thread trailing off the back fin.
animals.dan: Tarpon. The silver king. Scales as big as your palm and a mouth like a bucket. Hook one, and the whole fish leaves the water.
animals.book: The tournament’s main event.

animals.name: Redfish
animals.tell: Copper-bronze, blunt nose, a black spot at the base of the tail.
animals.dan: Redfish. Copper colored, with a black spot by the tail like a thumbprint. Some folks call him spot-tail. It was the first keeper Matt ever caught.
animals.book: The first keeper Matt ever caught, at Comer Key.

animals.name: Spotted seatrout
animals.tell: Slim and silver-gray, black dots over the back, fin and tail, two fangs up front.
animals.dan: Seatrout. Looks like somebody shook a pepper shaker over him. Soft mouth, so you never yank. Grass beds mean trout.
animals.book: ‘Grass bed fishing meant trout.’

animals.name: Mangrove snapper
animals.tell: Stocky and gray-bronze, a dark stripe through the eye, real teeth.
animals.dan: Mangrove snapper. Gray-bronze, with a dark stripe through the eye like a bandit’s mask. They call him snapper for a reason. Mind your fingers.
animals.book: The snapper bonanza at the river mouth.

animals.name: Sheepshead
animals.tell: Bold black-and-white bars straight up and down, and teeth that look human.
animals.dan: Sheepshead. Striped like an old-time convict, with a mouthful of teeth that look like yours. Best bait thief on any dock.

more.draw: a close-up of the head of a sheepshead fish with its mouth open, seen from the front and side: black and silver vertical bars, and a mouth full of broad, flat, human-looking front teeth with rows of rounded molar-like teeth behind

animals.name: Black drum
animals.tell: Shaped like a redfish but gray, no tail spot, whiskers under the chin.
animals.dan: Black drum. The redfish’s gray cousin. No spot on the tail, and whiskers under his chin for feeling out crabs in the mud.
animals.book: The single black drum in the Rabbit Key cooler.

animals.name: Flounder
animals.tell: Flat as a plate, both eyes on the same side, colored like the sand.
animals.dan: Flounder. Flat as a dinner plate, with both eyes on one side of his head. He lies on the bottom looking like sand, and waits.

animals.name: Jack crevalle
animals.tell: Blunt bulldog forehead, yellowish tail, a black spot on the gill cover.
animals.dan: Jack crevalle. Bulldog forehead, yellowish tail, black spot on the gill. Pound for pound he pulls harder than anything in the bay.
animals.book: Jacks herding baitfish at South Point.

animals.name: Ladyfish
animals.tell: Long, thin and bright silver, and in the air more than the water.
animals.dan: Ladyfish. Skinny, silver, and she spends the whole fight jumping. Fun to catch. Slippery as soap to hold.

animals.name: Mullet
animals.tell: Blunt nose, silver with faint stripes, and it jumps for no reason anyone has proven.
animals.dan: Mullet. Blunt nose, silver, and he jumps for no reason anybody’s ever proven. You won’t hook him, but everything you want eats him.
animals.book: The baitfish the Bagley Mullet lure imitates.

animals.name: Pinfish
animals.tell: Hand-sized, thin gold and blue stripes, a row of needle spines on the back.
animals.dan: Pinfish. Hand-sized, with a row of needles down his back. That’s bait, son. Hold him from underneath.

animals.name: Hardhead catfish
animals.tell: Whiskers, slick gray skin, and three stiff spines: one on top, one on each side.
animals.dan: Hardhead catfish. Whiskers and three sharp spines that sting. Don’t grab him. Use the pliers.
animals.book: The spiny catfish Matt caught as a kid off the motel dock.

animals.name: Pufferfish
animals.tell: Small and blotchy, with a beak, and it blows up like a ball when upset.
animals.dan: Pufferfish. Get him mad and he blows up like a prickly ball. Got a beak that’ll clip your hook, too. And never eat one. He’s poison.
animals.book: ‘Those little puffy buggers were tough to unhook.’

animals.name: Bonefish
animals.tell: Silver torpedo with a pointed nose and a mouth underneath, tailing in inches of water.
animals.dan: Bonefish. The gray ghost. Silver, with his mouth tucked underneath. He feeds in water so thin his tail sticks out.
animals.book: The fish Snapper once put a president on, down in the Keys.

animals.name: Cobia
animals.tell: Long and dark brown with a flat head and a pale stripe: looks like a shark at first glance.
animals.dan: Cobia. Long, brown, flat head. Half the people who see one yell shark. Look for the pale stripe down his side.
animals.book: A tournament category at Port of the Everglades.

animals.name: Gag grouper
animals.tell: Wide head, huge mouth, thick body in blotchy brown-gray camouflage.
animals.dan: Grouper. Big head, bigger mouth, blotchy like camouflage. Hook him and he has one plan: get back under his rock.
animals.book: Matt’s favorite eating fish.

animals.name: Yellowtail snapper
animals.tell: A yellow stripe from the nose straight into a forked yellow tail.
animals.dan: Yellowtail snapper. Follow the yellow stripe from his nose and it runs right into a forked yellow tail. Reef fish. Good eating.

animals.name: Amberjack
animals.tell: Big and bronze, with a dark stripe running from the nose up through the eye.
animals.dan: Amberjack. Big bronze brute off the wrecks. See the dark stripe from his nose up through his eye? They call him the reef donkey, because he pulls like one.

animals.name: Lionfish
animals.tell: Red-and-white zebra stripes and a fan of long spines that sting.
animals.dan: Lionfish. Zebra stripes and a fan of spines that’ll sting you good. Pretty, and he doesn’t belong here. He eats the reef’s baby fish.
animals.book: The newspaper story about animals that don’t belong here.

animals.name: Bluegill
animals.tell: Round as a saucer, small mouth, a dark flap behind the gill.
animals.dan: Bluegill. Round as a saucer, with a dark flap behind the gill. Folks call him brim. First fish most kids ever catch.

animals.name: Permit
animals.tell: Tall, flat and silver, blunt forehead, long dark sickle fins.
animals.dan: Permit. Tall, flat and silver, with long dark fins like sickles. The pickiest fish on the flats. Guides brag about one for a year.
animals.draw: a permit (Trachinotus falcatus): a tall, flat, silvery fish with a blunt rounded forehead, long dark sickle-shaped dorsal and anal fins, a deeply forked dark tail and a faint orange-yellow patch on the belly ahead of the anal fin

animals.name: Pompano
animals.tell: Like a small permit: silver with a yellow throat and belly and short fins.
animals.dan: Pompano. Looks like a permit’s little brother. Yellow on the throat and belly, shorter fins. He runs the beach in the surf.
animals.draw: a Florida pompano (Trachinotus carolinus): a small, flat, silvery fish with a rounded blunt head, a yellow throat and belly, short dorsal and anal fins and a forked tail; clearly smaller and shorter-finned than a permit

animals.name: Spanish mackerel
animals.tell: Slim and silver with gold oval spots on its sides and a black patch on the front fin.
animals.dan: Spanish mackerel. Slim, silver, with gold spots down his side. Teeth like razors. Bring pliers.
animals.draw: a Spanish mackerel (Scomberomorus maculatus): a slim, streamlined silver fish with a blue-green back, many yellow-gold oval spots along the sides, a black patch at the front of the first dorsal fin, small finlets before a deeply forked tail

animals.name: King mackerel
animals.tell: A bigger, plain silver mackerel: no spots, and the line on its side dips sharply.
animals.dan: King mackerel. Kingfish. Bigger than the Spanish and no gold spots. Look at the line on his side: it takes a sharp dip.
animals.draw: a king mackerel (Scomberomorus cavalla): a long, streamlined, plain silver fish with an iridescent blue-green back, no spots, a lateral line that drops sharply below the second dorsal fin, small finlets and a deeply forked tail

animals.name: Tripletail
animals.tell: Deep and mottled brown, with back fins so round it seems to have three tails.
animals.dan: Tripletail. Count the tails: looks like three. He floats on his side by a crab trap buoy, pretending to be a leaf.
animals.draw: an Atlantic tripletail (Lobotes surinamensis): a deep-bodied, mottled brown-and-tan fish whose rounded rear dorsal fin and anal fin reach back beside the rounded tail so it appears to have three tails; small head with a sloping forehead

animals.name: Barracuda
animals.tell: A long silver torpedo with an underbite full of fangs and dark blotches near the tail.
animals.dan: Barracuda. A silver torpedo with an underbite full of fangs. He’ll follow the boat just to look at you. Don’t dangle anything shiny.
animals.draw: a great barracuda (Sphyraena barracuda): a very long, slender silver fish with a pointed head, a jutting lower jaw full of visible fang-like teeth, a few dark blotches on the lower sides near the tail, and a forked tail

animals.name: Goliath grouper
animals.tell: A giant: brownish-yellow with small dark spots, tiny eyes and a round tail.
animals.dan: Goliath grouper. Big as a refrigerator, with little bitty eyes and a round tail. He’ll eat the fish right off your line and never say thank you.
animals.book: The unseen giant that dragged an anchored boat across the channel.
animals.draw: a goliath grouper (Epinephelus itajara): an enormous, very thick-bodied grouper, brownish-yellow with small dark spots on the head and fins, tiny eyes, a huge mouth, rounded fins and a rounded tail

animals.name: Red snapper
animals.tell: Rosy red all over, red eye, pointed fin underneath: a deep-water snapper.
animals.dan: Red snapper. Rosy red from nose to tail, even his eye. He lives deep, way offshore, and everybody wants him for supper.
animals.draw: a red snapper (Lutjanus campechanus): a stocky snapper that is rosy red all over, paler on the belly, with a red eye, a sloping forehead, a long pointed anal fin and a slightly forked tail

animals.name: Hogfish
animals.tell: A long pig-like snout and three long streamers on the front of the back fin.
animals.dan: Hogfish. Long snout like a pig, for rooting in the sand, and three long streamers on his back. Prettiest thing on the reef.
animals.draw: a hogfish (Lachnolaimus maximus): a deep-bodied reef fish with a long, sloping pig-like snout, reddish-orange and pearly mottled colour, the first three dorsal spines extended as long streamers, and a dark spot at the rear base of the dorsal fin

animals.name: Mahi-mahi
animals.tell: Electric green and gold with blue spots, one long fin from head to tail, a blunt square forehead.
animals.dan: Mahi-mahi. Some call him dolphin, but he’s no relation to Flipper. Green and gold like a neon sign, and a forehead like a brick.
animals.draw: a bull mahi-mahi or dolphinfish (Coryphaena hippurus): a long, tapering fish, brilliant green-gold with small blue spots, a single long blue dorsal fin running from the head almost to the tail, a tall blunt square forehead and a deeply forked tail

animals.name: Sailfish
animals.tell: A long spear for a nose and a giant blue sail on its back.
animals.dan: Sailfish. A spear on his nose and a blue sail on his back that he raises like a flag. Florida’s own saltwater fish. Fast as a pickup truck.
animals.draw: an Atlantic sailfish (Istiophorus albicans): a long, slender billfish with a long pointed spear-like bill, a huge cobalt-blue sail-like dorsal fin with dark spots raised high, a dark blue back, silver-white belly with faint vertical bars and a crescent tail

animals.name: Wahoo
animals.tell: Long and slim with blue tiger stripes down its sides and a pointed beak of a snout.
animals.dan: Wahoo. Tiger stripes down his sides and a snout like a beak. When he takes the bait, the reel screams, and so does everybody on the boat.
animals.draw: a wahoo (Acanthocybium solandri): a very long, slim, streamlined fish with a pointed beak-like snout, a steel-blue back and silver sides crossed by many vivid blue vertical tiger-like bars, small finlets and a forked tail

animals.name: Blackfin tuna
animals.tell: Shaped like a football: dark back, bronze stripe along the side, tiny fins near the tail.
animals.dan: Blackfin tuna. Built like a football that somebody taught to swim. Dark back, a bronze stripe on his side, and he never stops moving.
animals.draw: a blackfin tuna (Thunnus atlanticus): a compact, football-shaped tuna with a blue-black back, a bronze-gold band along the upper side, a silver-white belly, a row of small dusky finlets before a crescent tail

animals.name: Triggerfish
animals.tell: Flat, oval and leathery gray, tiny mouth with chisel teeth, a spine on top that locks upright.
animals.dan: Triggerfish. Flat, gray and tough as a boot. The spine on his back locks straight up, and only he knows where the trigger is.
animals.draw: a gray triggerfish (Balistes capriscus): a flat, oval, olive-gray fish with tough leathery skin, a small mouth with chisel teeth set at the tip of a long face, a stout first dorsal spine standing upright, and tall rear fins

animals.name: Largemouth bass
animals.tell: Green with a dark jagged stripe down the side and a mouth that reaches back past the eye.
animals.dan: Largemouth bass. Green, with a dark jagged stripe down the side. Close his mouth and the jaw reaches back past his eye. King of every Florida lake.
animals.draw: a Florida largemouth bass (Micropterus salmoides): an olive-green freshwater fish with a dark, jagged horizontal stripe along each side, a pale belly, and a very large mouth whose upper jaw reaches back past the eye

animals.name: Peacock bass
animals.tell: Gold with three dark bars down its sides and a black spot ringed in gold on the tail.
animals.dan: Peacock bass. Gold, with three dark bars and a spot on his tail like the eye on a peacock feather. He lives in the canals down around Miami.
animals.draw: a butterfly peacock bass (Cichla ocellaris): a golden-yellow freshwater fish with three dark vertical bars on each side, an olive back, orange lower fins, a red eye and a black spot ringed with gold at the base of the tail

animals.name: Black crappie
animals.tell: Silver and covered in black speckles, with tall rounded fins top and bottom.
animals.dan: Black crappie. Speckled perch, we call him. Silver with black freckles all over, and a mouth as thin as paper. Go easy.
animals.draw: a black crappie (Pomoxis nigromaculatus): a deep, flat-sided silvery freshwater panfish covered in irregular black speckles and blotches, with tall rounded dorsal and anal fins of about equal size and a large thin mouth

animals.name: Florida gar
animals.tell: A long olive log with dark spots, armor-hard scales and a long snout full of needle teeth.
animals.dan: Gar. Looks like a log with a long toothy snout. His scales are hard as armor. He’s been swimming these waters since the dinosaurs.
animals.draw: a Florida gar (Lepisosteus platyrhincus): a long, cylindrical olive-brown freshwater fish with a long, broad snout full of needle-like teeth, hard diamond-shaped scales, round dark spots on the body and fins, and fins set far back near a rounded tail

animals.name: Bowfin
animals.tell: One long fin rippling down most of its back, a round tail, and a dark spot near the tail.
animals.dan: Bowfin. Mudfish. One long fin runs down most of his back, and there’s a dark spot by his tail. He can gulp air, so mud doesn’t bother him.
animals.draw: a bowfin (Amia calva): a long, cylindrical olive-brown freshwater fish with a single long low dorsal fin running most of the length of the back, a rounded tail with a dark spot ringed in orange near its upper base, and a bullet-shaped head

animals.name: Blue marlin
animals.tell: A giant with a round spear for a nose, a cobalt-blue back and a low, pointed back fin, not a sail.
animals.dan: Blue marlin. The biggest prize in the ocean. A spear on his nose like the sailfish, but look at his back: a low pointed fin, no sail. The big ones can weigh as much as a horse.
animals.draw: an Atlantic blue marlin (Makaira nigricans) in exact side view, head to the left: a massive billfish with a long, round, spear-like bill, a cobalt-blue back, silver-white belly with faint pale blue vertical stripes, a low, pointed first dorsal fin that is highest at the front and NOT a sail, and a tall crescent tail

animals.name: Swordfish
animals.tell: A long, flat, wide bill like a real sword, and a huge eye for hunting in the deep dark.
animals.dan: Swordfish. His bill is flat and wide like a broadsword, where the marlin’s is round like a spear. And look at the size of that eye. He hunts way down deep, where it’s dark as midnight.
animals.draw: a swordfish (Xiphias gladius) in exact side view, head to the left: a large, stout, dark bronze-black fish with a pale belly, a very long, flat, broad sword-like bill, a very large eye, a tall curved crescent first dorsal fin, no pelvic fins, and a wide crescent tail

animals.name: Yellowfin tuna
animals.tell: A big tuna with bright yellow fins, and two long yellow sickles on its back and belly.
animals.dan: Yellowfin tuna. Like the blackfin, only bigger, with fins as yellow as a school bus. The big ones grow two long yellow sickles, top and bottom.
animals.draw: a yellowfin tuna (Thunnus albacares) in exact side view, head to the left: a large torpedo-shaped tuna with a dark metallic blue back, a golden-yellow band along the side, a silver belly, bright yellow finlets, and very long, sickle-shaped bright yellow second dorsal and anal fins

animals.name: Red grouper
animals.tell: A rusty-red grouper with pale blotches and a mouth that is bright red-orange inside.
animals.dan: Red grouper. Rusty red with pale blotches. Open his mouth and it’s bright orange inside. He digs out his own hole in the bottom and keeps house there.
animals.draw: a red grouper (Epinephelus morio) in exact side view, head to the left, mouth slightly open: a stout, robust reddish-brown grouper with scattered pale whitish blotches, small dark specks around the eye, a squared-off tail, and a bright scarlet-orange lining visible inside the mouth

animals.name: Mutton snapper
animals.tell: A snapper with one small black dot on its upper side and thin blue lines on its cheek.
animals.dan: Mutton snapper. Look for one small black dot high on his side, and thin blue lines under his eye like war paint. Smart as a whip, too.
animals.draw: a mutton snapper (Lutjanus analis) in exact side view, head to the left: an olive-backed snapper with rosy-red lower sides and reddish fins, a single small black spot on the upper side just below the soft dorsal fin, thin blue lines on the cheek below the eye, and a pointed anal fin

animals.name: Flying fish
animals.tell: A small blue-and-silver fish with side fins as long as wings, gliding over the waves.
animals.dan: Flying fish. Yes sir, he flies. Blue back, silver belly, and fins like wings. Something chases him, and he pops out and glides clean over the waves. First time you see it, you won’t believe it.
animals.draw: an Atlantic flying fish gliding just above the wave tops, seen from the side and slightly above, head to the left: a slim fish with a dark blue back and silver belly, enormously long, transparent wing-like pectoral fins spread wide, a deeply forked tail with a longer lower lobe, and a few drops of water trailing

animals.name: Needlefish
animals.tell: As thin as a pencil and silver-green, with a long beak full of tiny needle teeth.
animals.dan: Needlefish. Skinny as a pencil, with a beak like a pair of needle-nose pliers. He hangs right at the surface under the dock light, and skips across the top when he’s spooked.
animals.draw: an Atlantic needlefish (Strongylura marina) in exact side view at the water’s surface, head to the left: an extremely long, slender, pencil-thin silvery-green fish with very long, narrow beak-like jaws lined with tiny needle teeth, and small fins set far back near the tail

animals.name: Remora
animals.tell: A slim dark fish with a flat sucker on top of its head, hitching a ride on a shark.
animals.dan: Remora. Sharksucker. See the flat pad on top of his head, like the sole of a sneaker? That’s a suction cup. He sticks himself to a shark and rides for free, eating the scraps.
animals.draw: a remora or sharksucker (Echeneis naucrates) in side view tilted slightly so the top of the head shows, head to the left: a slim, elongated gray fish with a dark stripe along the side edged in white, and a large, flat, oval ridged suction disc on top of its head

animals.name: Green moray eel
animals.tell: A thick green eel with no side fins, poking out of a hole in the reef with its mouth open.
animals.dan: Green moray. A fat green eel looking out of a hole in the reef with his mouth hanging open. He’s not mad. That’s just how he breathes. But here’s a rule for life: never stick your hand in a hole.
animals.draw: a green moray eel (Gymnothorax funebris) emerging from a crevice in a coral reef, the front half of its body showing: a thick, muscular, uniformly yellowish-green eel with no pectoral fins, a continuous fin along the back, small eyes, and its mouth held open showing pointed teeth

animals.name: Parrotfish
animals.tell: Bright blue and green, with teeth fused into a beak like a parrot’s.
animals.dan: Parrotfish. Blue and green like a parrot, with a beak to match. He bites off chunks of coral, grinds them up, and what comes out the other end is sand. A good bit of that white beach came out of a parrotfish.
animals.draw: a stoplight parrotfish, adult male (Sparisoma viride) in exact side view, head to the left: a stout, large-scaled reef fish, bright emerald green and turquoise with pink and yellow markings on the head and fins, a yellow spot at the gill cover and tail base, and teeth fused into a pale parrot-like beak

animals.name: Queen angelfish
animals.tell: A flat blue-and-yellow disc with a dark blue crown spot on its forehead and long trailing fins.
animals.dan: Queen angelfish. Blue and yellow, flat as a pancake standing on its edge, with a little blue crown on her forehead. That’s why she’s the queen.
animals.draw: a queen angelfish (Holacanthus ciliaris) in exact side view, head to the left: a very flat, disc-shaped reef fish, electric blue and bright yellow, with a round dark blue crown spot ringed in bright blue on the forehead, a yellow tail, and long trailing tips on the dorsal and anal fins

animals.name: Porcupinefish
animals.tell: A big-eyed puffer covered in long spines that stand straight out when it blows up.
animals.dan: Porcupinefish. A puffer with real spines. Blown up, he’s a pincushion the size of a basketball, with big sad eyes. Look, laugh, and leave him alone.
animals.draw: a porcupinefish (Diodon hystrix) inflated into a ball, in side view, head to the left: a round, pale tan fish with small dark spots, very large round eyes, a small beak-like mouth, and long sharp spines standing straight out all over its body

animals.name: Snakehead
animals.tell: Long and dark with a flat, snaky head, one long fin above and one below, and an orange-ringed spot by the tail.
animals.dan: Snakehead. Head like a snake, one long fin on top and another underneath, and an orange-ringed spot by his tail. He’s from Asia, and he turned up in the canals of southeast Florida. He breathes air, and he eats everything.
animals.draw: a bullseye snakehead (Channa marulius) in exact side view, head to the left: a long, cylindrical dark olive-brown freshwater fish with a flattened snake-like head, a very long dorsal fin and a long anal fin running along most of the body, pale spots on the sides, and a black eyespot ringed in bright orange at the upper base of the tail

animals.name: Channel catfish
animals.tell: A smooth gray catfish with long whiskers, a deeply forked tail and a few dark spots.
animals.dan: Channel catfish. Freshwater cousin of the hardhead. Long whiskers, forked tail, a few dark spots on his sides. Same rule applies: mind the spines.
animals.draw: a channel catfish (Ictalurus punctatus) in exact side view, head to the left: a smooth-skinned, slender blue-gray freshwater catfish with a white belly, scattered small dark spots on the sides, long dark whisker-like barbels around the mouth, and a deeply forked tail

animals.name: Gulf sturgeon
animals.tell: A long, armor-plated fish with rows of bony bumps, whiskers under a long snout and a shark’s tail.
animals.dan: Gulf sturgeon. Looks like a dinosaur, because he very nearly is one. Rows of bony armor, whiskers under his nose. They come up the Suwannee River every spring, stay the summer, and jump clear out of the water, long as a canoe paddle and then some.
animals.draw: a Gulf sturgeon (Acipenser oxyrinchus desotoi) in exact side view, head to the left: a long, primitive brownish-gray fish with five rows of bony armor plates (scutes) along the body, a long flattened pointed snout with four short whisker-like barbels underneath ahead of the mouth, and a shark-like tail with a longer upper lobe

animals.name: Bull shark
animals.tell: Thick and plain gray, with a short, blunt, rounded snout and small eyes.
animals.dan: Bull shark. Thick, plain gray, with a short blunt nose. He’s the one that swims right up the rivers into fresh water. Give him room.
animals.draw: a bull shark (Carcharhinus leucas): a stocky, heavy-bodied plain gray shark with a white belly, a very short, broad, blunt rounded snout, small eyes, a large triangular first dorsal fin and no markings

animals.name: Blacktip shark
animals.tell: Slim, with a pointed snout, black tips on its fins and a pale stripe along the side.
animals.dan: Blacktip. Slim, pointed nose, and it looks like he dipped his fins in ink. He’ll jump clear out of the water and spin like a top.
animals.draw: a blacktip shark (Carcharhinus limbatus): a slim, streamlined gray-bronze shark with a long pointed snout, distinct black tips on the dorsal, pectoral and lower tail fins, a white belly and a pale white band along each flank

animals.name: Lemon shark
animals.tell: Yellowish-brown, with two back fins almost the same size.
animals.dan: Lemon shark. Yellowish, like the name says. Here’s the trick: look at the two fins on his back. They’re nearly the same size.
animals.draw: a lemon shark (Negaprion brevirostris): a stocky yellowish-brown shark with a pale yellow belly, a short blunt snout, and two dorsal fins of nearly equal size, the second almost as large as the first

animals.name: Nurse shark
animals.tell: Brown, lying on the bottom, with two whiskers by a small mouth and a long tail.
animals.dan: Nurse shark. Brown, sleepy, lying on the bottom with two little whiskers by his mouth. Laziest shark in Florida. Leave him be, and don’t pull his tail.
animals.draw: a nurse shark (Ginglymostoma cirratum): a smooth tan-brown shark resting near a sandy bottom, with a broad flat head, a small mouth with two fleshy barbels (whiskers) beneath the snout, rounded fins, two dorsal fins set far back and a very long tail

more.draw: a close-up of the face of a nurse shark seen from the front and slightly below: a broad, flat, tan-brown head with a small mouth and two fleshy whisker-like barbels hanging from the nostrils just in front of the mouth, small eyes

animals.name: Tiger shark
animals.tell: Gray, with dark bars down its sides that fade as it grows, and a very wide, square, blunt snout.
animals.dan: Tiger shark. Dark bars down his sides when he’s young, and a nose as wide and square as a shovel. He’ll eat anything. They’ve found license plates in there.
animals.draw: a tiger shark (Galeocerdo cuvier): a large gray shark with dark vertical tiger-like bars and blotches along its sides, a very broad, blunt, squared-off snout, a white belly and a long upper tail lobe

animals.name: Great hammerhead
animals.tell: A head shaped like a hammer and a back fin as tall as a sail.
animals.dan: Hammerhead. You won’t mix this one up. Head like a hammer, eyes way out on the ends, and a back fin tall as a sail.
animals.book: A hammerhead turns up when Matt least needs one.

more.cap: From above: a wide, nearly straight hammer.
more.draw: a great hammerhead shark seen from directly above, swimming: the very wide, flat, nearly straight-edged hammer-shaped head with an eye at each outer end and a small notch at the centre of the front edge, the tall dorsal fin and tapering gray body behind

animals.name: Bonnethead shark
animals.tell: A small shark with a head rounded like a shovel, not stretched out like a hammer.
animals.dan: Bonnethead. The hammerhead’s little cousin. Maybe a yard long, with a head rounded like a shovel. He eats crabs on the flats.
animals.draw: a bonnethead shark (Sphyrna tiburo): a small, slender gray-brown shark with a smoothly rounded, shovel-shaped flattened head with eyes at its outer edges, much narrower and rounder than a hammerhead’s, and a pale belly

more.draw: a bonnethead shark seen from directly above, swimming over a sandy flat: the small shark’s head is a smoothly rounded, shovel-shaped arc with an eye at each side, much narrower and rounder than a hammerhead’s, with a slender gray-brown body behind

animals.name: Mako shark
animals.tell: Sleek and metallic blue, a pointed cone of a snout, big black eyes, thin teeth that always show.
animals.dan: Mako. Blue as the deep water he lives in, with a pointed nose and teeth that show even when his mouth is shut. Fastest shark there is.
animals.book: The shark on the beach at Comer Key.

more.cap: Long, thin, curved teeth that show even with the mouth shut.
more.draw: a close-up of the head of a shortfin mako shark in side view with the mouth slightly open: a pointed, conical metallic-blue snout, a large round black eye, and long, slender, smooth-edged, curved dagger-like teeth protruding from the lower jaw, visible even though the mouth is nearly closed

animals.name: Great white shark
animals.tell: Heavy and torpedo-shaped: gray on top, white below, with a sharp line between and black eyes.
animals.dan: Great white. Heavy as a truck, gray on top and white below, with a sharp line between. He comes south in the winter, way offshore, like a snowbird.
animals.draw: a great white shark (Carcharodon carcharias): a massive, heavy torpedo-shaped shark, slate gray above and pure white below with a sharp jagged line between the two, a conical snout, black eyes, large triangular teeth, and a crescent tail

more.cap: Wide triangle teeth with saw edges.
more.draw: a close-up of the open jaws of a great white shark seen from the front and side: rows of large, broad, triangular white teeth with finely serrated saw-like edges, pink gums, the conical gray snout above

animals.name: Whale shark
animals.tell: The biggest fish alive: a checkerboard of white spots and a mouth as wide as a doorway.
animals.dan: Whale shark. Biggest fish in the whole ocean, covered in white spots like a checkerboard. And all he eats is tiny stuff. Gentle as a cow.
animals.draw: a whale shark (Rhincodon typus): an enormous shark with a broad flat head and a very wide mouth at the front, a blue-gray back covered in a checkerboard pattern of pale white spots and stripes, ridges along the body and a white belly

animals.name: Thresher shark
animals.tell: A tail as long as the whole rest of its body, curved like a scythe.
animals.dan: Thresher shark. Look at that tail. It’s as long as the rest of him. He cracks it like a whip to knock fish silly, then circles back to eat them.
animals.draw: a common thresher shark (Alopias vulpinus) in exact side view, head to the left: a sleek blue-gray shark with a white belly, a short conical snout, big eyes, long pectoral fins, and an enormously long, scythe-shaped upper tail lobe as long as the rest of the body

animals.name: Spinner shark
animals.tell: Slim, with a long pointed snout and a black tip on every fin, even the small one underneath.
animals.dan: Spinner shark. The blacktip’s twin, nearly. Longer nose, and a black tip on every single fin. He comes up through a school of bait spinning like a drill and jumps clear out of the water.
animals.draw: a spinner shark (Carcharhinus brevipinna) in exact side view, head to the left: a slender gray-bronze shark with a very long, pointed snout, small eyes, and distinct black tips on ALL fins including the dorsal fins, pectoral fins, pelvic fins, the small anal fin underneath and the lower tail lobe, with a faint pale band on the flank

animals.name: Sharpnose shark
animals.tell: A small gray-brown shark with a long, flat, pointed snout and a scatter of small white spots.
animals.dan: Sharpnose shark. A little fellow, maybe a yard long, with a long pointed nose and white freckles on his sides. Most of the small sharks you’ll catch off the beach are him.
animals.draw: an Atlantic sharpnose shark (Rhizoprionodon terraenovae) in exact side view, head to the left: a small, slender gray-brown shark with a long, flattened, pointed snout, large eyes, a white belly, small scattered white spots on the sides, and a dusky edge on the dorsal fin

animals.name: Sandbar shark
animals.tell: A brownish-gray shark with a very tall, triangular back fin set far forward.
animals.dan: Sandbar shark. See how tall that back fin is? Like a sail, and set way up front over his shoulders. That’s the fin they put in the movies.
animals.draw: a sandbar shark (Carcharhinus plumbeus) in exact side view, head to the left: a stout brownish-gray shark with a white belly, a rounded snout, and a very tall, large triangular first dorsal fin set far forward above the pectoral fins, with no markings

animals.name: Reef shark
animals.tell: A sturdy gray shark of the coral reef, with dusky edges on its fins and a dark edge on its tail.
animals.dan: Caribbean reef shark. He’s the gray shark the divers see cruising the coral down in the Keys. No stripes, no spots, just a dusky edge on his fins and tail. He owns that reef, and he knows it.
animals.draw: a Caribbean reef shark (Carcharhinus perezi) in exact side view over a coral reef edge, head to the left: a sturdy, streamlined dark gray shark with a white belly, a short rounded snout, dusky darker edges on the pectoral, pelvic and anal fins and a dark trailing edge on the tail, with no stripes or spots

animals.name: Southern stingray
animals.tell: A flat brown diamond with a whip of a tail, half-buried in the sand.
animals.dan: Stingray. A flat brown diamond with a whip for a tail and a barb on it. He hides in the sand, so shuffle your feet when you wade.
animals.draw: a southern stingray (Hypanus americanus) seen from above: a flat, diamond-shaped olive-brown ray with pointed wing tips, eyes and spiracles on top of the head, and a long thin whip-like tail with a barb

animals.name: Manta ray
animals.tell: Huge wings, black on top and white below, with two horn-like flaps beside its mouth.
animals.dan: Manta ray. Wings as wide as a boat, black on top, white below, with two flaps by his mouth like horns. No stinger. He just flies along, eating soup.
animals.draw: a giant manta ray (Mobula birostris) seen from above and slightly in front: a huge ray with long triangular wing-like fins, a black back with pale shoulder patches, a white underside, a wide mouth at the front flanked by two horn-like head flaps, and a short thin tail with no barb

animals.name: Spotted eagle ray
animals.tell: A dark ray covered in white spots and rings, with pointed wings and a very long whip tail.
animals.dan: Spotted eagle ray. Dark back covered in white spots and rings, and a snout like a duck’s bill. He flies through the water like a bird, and now and then he jumps clean out of it.
animals.draw: a spotted eagle ray (Aetobatus narinari) seen from above and slightly to the side, swimming: a ray with long, pointed wing-like fins, a dark brown back covered in white spots and rings, a white underside, a distinct head with a flat duck-bill-like snout, and a very long thin whip tail

animals.name: Sawfish
animals.tell: A long flat snout like a saw, with teeth down both edges.
animals.dan: Sawfish. A snout like a hedge trimmer, teeth down both sides. There aren’t many left, and the Everglades is their nursery. See one, and you’ve seen something.
animals.draw: a smalltooth sawfish (Pristis pectinata): a long, flattened shark-like ray, olive-brown above and white below, with a very long, flat, blade-like snout edged on both sides with evenly spaced teeth like a saw, and two tall dorsal fins

animals.name: Oceanic whitetip shark
animals.tell: Long, rounded fins like paddles, each one tipped in mottled white, far out in blue water.
animals.dan: Oceanic whitetip. He lives way out in the blue water. Long round fins like canoe paddles, tipped in white like he brushed against wet paint.
animals.draw: an oceanic whitetip shark (Carcharhinus longimanus) in exact side view, head to the left: a stocky bronze-gray shark with a white belly, a short blunt snout, and very long, broad, rounded paddle-like pectoral fins and a tall rounded first dorsal fin, each with mottled white tips

animals.name: Sand tiger shark
animals.tell: A mouthful of long, ragged teeth sticking out every which way, and two back fins the same size.
animals.dan: Sand tiger. Scariest smile in the ocean: long snaggle teeth sticking out every which way. It’s mostly show. He’s a mellow shark, as sharks go. Still, you look, you don’t touch.
animals.draw: a sand tiger shark (Carcharias taurus) in exact side view, head to the left: a bulky light brown shark with scattered darker reddish-brown spots, a pointed flattened snout, a mouth held slightly open showing long, narrow, ragged protruding teeth, small eyes, and two dorsal fins of about equal size set far back

animals.name: Cownose ray
animals.tell: A brown ray with a notched, squared-off forehead like a cow’s nose, traveling in big schools.
animals.dan: Cownose ray. Brown, with a dented forehead like a cow’s nose. They come down the coast by the hundreds, and their wingtips poke up like shark fins. Scares a lot of tourists.
animals.draw: a cownose ray (Rhinoptera bonasus) seen from above and slightly to the side, swimming: a plain golden-brown ray with pointed wing-like fins, a distinctly notched, squared-off double-lobed forehead like a cow’s nose, a whitish underside and a long thin tail

animals.name: Alligator
animals.tell: Dark, almost black, with a wide rounded snout shaped like a U. Mouth shut, only top teeth show.
animals.dan: Alligator. Dark, nearly black, with a wide round snout like the letter U. Fresh water is his home. Never, ever feed one.
animals.book: The grouper thief at Lostman’s River.
animals.draw: an American alligator (Alligator mississippiensis) in side view on a mud bank, head to the left: dark blackish-gray, heavily armored, with a broad, rounded U-shaped snout, and with the mouth closed only the upper teeth visible

more.cap: From above: wide and rounded, like the letter U.
more.draw: the head of an American alligator seen from directly above, mouth closed, floating at the water’s surface: dark blackish-gray, with a broad, wide, rounded U-shaped snout, the nostrils and eyes raised above the water

animals.name: Crocodile
animals.tell: Lighter gray-green, with a narrow pointed snout shaped like a V. Mouth shut, teeth show top and bottom.
animals.dan: Crocodile. Lighter colored, with a narrow pointed snout like the letter V, and teeth showing top and bottom. He likes salty water, down at the south tip of Florida, where you can find gators and crocs both. Give him room.
animals.draw: an American crocodile (Crocodylus acutus) in side view on a sandy bank, head to the left: light grayish-green to tan, with a long, narrow, tapering V-shaped snout, and with the mouth closed teeth from both the upper and the lower jaw visible, including a large lower tooth near the front

more.cap: From above: narrow and pointed, like the letter V.
more.draw: the head of an American crocodile seen from directly above, mouth closed, floating at the water’s surface: light grayish-green, with a long, narrow, tapering V-shaped pointed snout, and teeth of the lower jaw visible along the outside edge of the closed mouth

animals.name: Cottonmouth
animals.tell: Thick and dark, with a blocky head and a dark band through the eye; it opens a cotton-white mouth as a warning.
animals.dan: Cottonmouth. Water moccasin. Thick, dark, with a head like a brick. When he’s had enough of you he opens his mouth, and it’s white as cotton. He’s venomous, and that’s your invitation to leave.
animals.book: The snake drawn to the lantern at Comer Key.
animals.draw: a cottonmouth or water moccasin (Agkistrodon conanti) coiled at the water’s edge with its mouth open wide in a warning gape showing the cotton-white lining: a thick, heavy-bodied dark olive-brown snake with faint darker bands, a broad blocky head and a dark band through the eye

more.cap: Swimming, most of its thick body rides on top of the water.
more.draw: a cottonmouth (water moccasin) swimming across calm dark water seen from the side and slightly above: a thick, heavy dark olive-brown snake floating high so that its whole body rides on top of the water surface, the blocky head held up at an angle, with a dark band through the eye

animals.name: Banded water snake
animals.tell: A slimmer brown snake with dark bands and a narrow head with round eyes. Not venomous, and always mistaken for a moccasin.
animals.dan: Banded water snake. Slimmer than a moccasin, narrow head, round eyes. Not venomous. But you don’t need to sort them out up close. Leave every snake alone, and you’ll never be wrong.
animals.draw: a banded water snake (Nerodia fasciata): a medium-sized, moderately slender brown snake with dark reddish-brown crossbands along its body, a narrow head barely wider than the neck, round pupils and dark vertical lines on the lip scales, on a wet bank

more.cap: Swimming, usually only its head shows.
more.draw: a banded water snake swimming across calm water seen from the side and slightly above: a slimmer brown banded snake with most of its body under the surface and only its narrow head and a little of its neck above the water

animals.name: Coral snake
animals.tell: Rings of red, yellow and black, with the red touching the yellow, and a black nose.
animals.dan: Coral snake. Red, yellow and black rings, and a black nose. Here’s the rhyme my daddy taught me: red touches yellow, dangerous fellow. Look, and walk away.
animals.draw: an eastern coral snake (Micrurus fulvius): a slender, glossy snake with a BLACK snout and complete rings around the body in this exact order: wide red ring, narrow yellow ring, wide black ring, narrow yellow ring, wide red ring, so that every red ring touches yellow rings on both sides and red never touches black

more.cap: Black nose. Every red ring touches yellow.
more.draw: a close-up of the head and front third of an eastern coral snake on leaf litter: a completely BLACK snout and front of the head, then a wide yellow band across the back of the head, then a wide black ring, a narrow yellow ring, a wide red ring, a narrow yellow ring, a wide black ring: the red rings are bordered by yellow on both sides and never touch black

animals.name: Scarlet kingsnake
animals.tell: Rings of red, black and yellow, with the red touching the black, and a red nose.
animals.dan: Scarlet kingsnake. He wears the coral snake’s colors, but in a different order, and his nose is red. Red touches black, friend of Jack. Not venomous. Still, hands off.
animals.draw: a scarlet kingsnake (Lampropeltis elapsoides): a small, slender, glossy snake with a RED snout and rings around the body in this exact order: wide red ring, narrow black ring, narrow yellow ring, narrow black ring, wide red ring, so that every red ring touches black rings on both sides and red never touches yellow

more.cap: Red nose. Every red ring touches black.
more.draw: a close-up of the head and front third of a scarlet kingsnake on leaf litter: a RED snout and red top of the head, then a narrow black ring, a narrow yellow ring, a narrow black ring, a wide red ring, a narrow black ring, a narrow yellow ring: the red rings are bordered by black on both sides and never touch yellow

animals.name: Diamondback rattlesnake
animals.tell: Big and heavy, with dark diamonds outlined in cream down its back and a rattle on its tail.
animals.dan: Eastern diamondback. Biggest rattlesnake there is. Dark diamonds down his back, and a rattle on the end. When you hear that buzz, freeze, then back away slow. Don’t go looking for him.
animals.draw: an eastern diamondback rattlesnake (Crotalus adamanteus) coiled: a large, heavy-bodied snake with a row of dark brown diamonds outlined in cream down its back, a broad head with two pale diagonal stripes on the face, and a segmented rattle at the tip of the tail

more.draw: a close-up of the tail tip of an eastern diamondback rattlesnake raised off the ground: the last black-and-white ringed section of the tail ending in a segmented, tan, horny rattle of about ten interlocking segments

animals.name: Pygmy rattlesnake
animals.tell: Small and gray with dark blotches, a rusty stripe down the back and a tiny rattle.
animals.dan: Pygmy rattler. Not much longer than your forearm. Gray with dark blotches and a rusty stripe down the back. His rattle’s so small it sounds like a bug. He’s venomous, so watch where you put your hands.
animals.draw: a dusky pygmy rattlesnake (Sistrurus miliarius): a small, fairly stout gray snake with a row of dark rounded blotches down the back, a thin rusty-orange stripe along the spine between the blotches, and a very tiny rattle at the tail tip

animals.name: Corn snake
animals.tell: Orange, with red-brown blotches outlined in black down its back. Not venomous.
animals.dan: Corn snake. Orange with red blotches outlined in black. Some call him the red rat snake, because that’s what he eats. A good neighbor to have around a barn.
animals.draw: a corn snake or red rat snake (Pantherophis guttatus): a slender orange snake with a row of large red-brown blotches outlined in black down its back, smaller blotches on the sides, and a spear-shaped mark on top of the head

animals.name: Black racer
animals.tell: Slim, plain satin black, with a white chin, and gone before you can point.
animals.dan: Black racer. Skinny, plain black, white chin, and fast. By the time you say there’s a snake, he’s in the next county. Not venomous. Let him go.
animals.draw: a southern black racer (Coluber constrictor priapus): a long, very slender, smooth matte satin-black snake with a white chin and throat and large eyes, stretched out alert on leaf litter

animals.name: Indigo snake
animals.tell: Very long and thick, glossy blue-black like polished metal, often with a reddish chin.
animals.dan: Indigo snake. Long as a canoe paddle and thick as your wrist, shiny blue-black like a new truck. Gentle, and getting rare. If you see one, count yourself lucky.
animals.draw: an eastern indigo snake (Drymarchon couperi): a very large, thick-bodied snake with glossy, iridescent blue-black scales like polished metal and a reddish-orange chin and throat

animals.name: Burmese python
animals.tell: A giant: tan with dark brown blotches like a giraffe’s, as thick as a grown man’s leg.
animals.dan: Burmese python. Tan with brown blotches like a giraffe, and as big around as a grown man’s leg. He doesn’t belong in the Everglades. Somebody’s pet got loose, and now there are thousands.
animals.draw: a Burmese python (Python bivittatus): a giant, very thick-bodied snake, tan with large dark brown giraffe-like blotches bordered in black along the back and sides, and a dark arrowhead mark on top of the head, lying in sawgrass

animals.name: Yellow rat snake
animals.tell: Long and yellowish, with four dark stripes running the whole length of its body.
animals.dan: Yellow rat snake. Long, yellow, with four dark stripes from his neck to his tail. Chicken snake, we call him. Best climber in the woods. He’ll go straight up a tree trunk. Not venomous.
animals.draw: a yellow rat snake (Pantherophis alleghaniensis, Florida yellow form) climbing a pine trunk: a long, fairly slender golden-yellow to tan snake with four distinct dark brown stripes running lengthwise from neck to tail, a pale chin and a yellowish eye

animals.name: Garter snake
animals.tell: Slim and dark, with three pale stripes from head to tail and a checkered pattern between them.
animals.dan: Garter snake. Three pale stripes down a dark body, one on top and one down each side. In Florida the stripes often run a little blue. The first snake most kids ever meet. Not venomous. Let him go on his way.
animals.draw: an eastern garter snake (Thamnophis sirtalis) in grass: a slim dark olive-brown snake with three pale yellowish to bluish-green stripes running the length of the body, one down the middle of the back and one along each side, with a checkered pattern of dark spots between the stripes

animals.name: Rough green snake
animals.tell: As thin as a pencil and bright leaf-green all over the top, with a pale yellow belly.
animals.dan: Rough green snake. Thin as a pencil and green as a new leaf. He lives up in the bushes and vines, eating crickets, and you’ll walk past ten for every one you see. Gentle as they come. Not venomous.
animals.draw: a rough green snake (Opheodrys aestivus) stretched along a leafy vine: a very slender, long snake that is uniformly bright leaf-green above with a pale yellow-white belly and chin, a small narrow head and large eyes

animals.name: Ringneck snake
animals.tell: A tiny slate-gray snake with a bright orange-yellow ring around its neck and an orange belly.
animals.dan: Ringneck snake. No bigger than a pencil, dark gray, with a bright ring around his neck like a collar. Scare him and he curls up his tail to show you an orange belly. You’ll find him under a flowerpot.
animals.draw: a southern ringneck snake (Diadophis punctatus punctatus) on leaf litter with its tail curled into a corkscrew showing the underside: a very small, slender, smooth slate-gray to black snake with a bright yellow-orange ring around the neck and a bright yellow-orange belly turning red under the tail, with a row of small black spots down the belly

animals.name: Hognose snake
animals.tell: A stout, blotchy snake with a turned-up nose like a little shovel, spreading its neck flat like a cobra.
animals.dan: Hognose snake. Turned-up nose like a pig. Now here’s the best actor in Florida. Bother him and he flattens his neck like a cobra and hisses. If that doesn’t work, he rolls over and plays dead with his tongue hanging out. It’s all an act. Leave him to it.
animals.draw: an eastern hognose snake (Heterodon platirhinos) on sandy ground with its neck flattened and spread wide like a cobra hood: a stout, thick-bodied snake, tan-yellow with dark brown blotches down the back, with a distinctly upturned, pointed shovel-like snout

animals.name: Copperhead
animals.tell: Tan, with dark bands shaped like hourglasses and a plain copper-colored head. In Florida, only in the Panhandle.
animals.dan: Copperhead. Tan, with dark bands pinched in the middle like an hourglass, and a head the color of a new penny. In Florida you’ll only find him up in the Panhandle. He’s venomous, and he hides in dead leaves, so watch your feet.
animals.draw: a copperhead (Agkistrodon contortrix) coiled on dead oak leaves: a stout pinkish-tan snake with a series of dark chestnut-brown crossbands shaped like hourglasses, narrow across the top of the back and wide on the sides, and a plain, unmarked coppery-orange triangular head

animals.name: Timber rattlesnake
animals.tell: Pinkish-gray, with black V-shaped bands, a rusty stripe down the spine and a solid black tail ending in a rattle.
animals.dan: Timber rattlesnake. Canebrake, the old folks say. Black bands shaped like a V, a rusty stripe down his backbone, and a black velvet tail with a rattle on it. North Florida woods and river swamps. Venomous. Back away slow.
animals.draw: a timber rattlesnake, canebrake form (Crotalus horridus) coiled: a large, heavy pinkish-gray to tan snake with black chevron or V-shaped crossbands, a rusty reddish-brown stripe running down the middle of the back, a dark stripe from the eye to the jaw, and a solid velvety black tail ending in a segmented rattle

animals.name: Green iguana
animals.tell: A big lizard with a row of spines down its back, a flap under its chin and a long striped tail.
animals.dan: Green iguana. Long as a canoe paddle, tail and all, with spines down his back and a flap under his chin. He’s not from here either. On a cold morning they fall right out of the trees.
animals.book: The newspaper story about animals that don’t belong here.
animals.draw: a green iguana (Iguana iguana) on a branch in side view: a large green lizard with a row of tall spines along its neck and back, a big dewlap flap under the chin, a large round scale on the cheek, and a very long tail with dark bands

animals.name: Green anole
animals.tell: A finger-long bright green lizard that fans out a pink flap under its throat.
animals.dan: Green anole. Little green lizard, long as your finger, on every porch rail in Florida. Watch him puff out that pink throat to show off.
animals.draw: a green anole (Anolis carolinensis) on a fence rail in side view: a small, slender bright green lizard with a long pointed snout and a long thin tail, extending a pink fan-shaped throat flap (dewlap)

animals.name: Gopher tortoise
animals.tell: A land tortoise with a high brown dome and front legs like shovels.
animals.dan: Gopher tortoise. He lives on land, not in the water. High domed shell and front legs like shovels. He digs a burrow that a hundred other critters move into.
animals.draw: a gopher tortoise (Gopherus polyphemus) on sandy ground in side view: a land tortoise with a high, domed gray-brown shell with growth rings, a blunt head, and broad, flattened shovel-like front legs with heavy scales and thick claws

animals.name: Loggerhead sea turtle
animals.tell: A sea turtle with a reddish-brown shell and a big, blocky head.
animals.dan: Loggerhead. Sea turtle with a head like a block of wood, built for crunching crabs. The mamas crawl up Florida’s beaches on summer nights to lay their eggs.
animals.draw: a loggerhead sea turtle (Caretta caretta) swimming in side view: a sea turtle with a reddish-brown heart-shaped shell, a very large, broad, blocky head with strong jaws, yellowish skin on the neck and flippers

animals.name: Green sea turtle
animals.tell: A sea turtle with a smooth shell streaked like a sunburst and a small, rounded head.
animals.dan: Green sea turtle. Small round head and a smooth shell with streaks like a sunburst. He grazes on seagrass like a cow in a pasture.
animals.draw: a green sea turtle (Chelonia mydas) swimming in side view over seagrass: a sea turtle with a smooth, oval olive-brown shell marked with radiating sunburst streaks, a small rounded head with a short blunt beak, and scales on the head outlined in pale yellow

animals.name: Softshell turtle
animals.tell: A flat, leathery shell like a pancake and a long nose like a snorkel.
animals.dan: Softshell turtle. Flat as a pancake, with a leathery shell and a nose like a snorkel. Long neck, too, and he can reach around and bite. Hands off the pancake.
animals.draw: a Florida softshell turtle (Apalone ferox) in side-and-above view at the water’s edge: a turtle with a flat, leathery, pancake-like olive-brown shell with no hard scutes, a long neck, and a long tubular snorkel-like snout

animals.name: Kingsnake
animals.tell: A sturdy dark snake crossed by thin pale bands, each scale tipped light so it looks speckled.
animals.dan: Kingsnake. Dark, with pale bands. Know why he’s the king? He eats other snakes. Rattlesnakes included. Their venom doesn’t bother him one bit. Not venomous himself.
animals.draw: a Florida kingsnake (Lampropeltis getula floridana) on sandy ground: a sturdy, medium-large snake with smooth glossy scales, dark brown to black with many thin pale yellowish crossbands, each dark scale having a pale base so the whole snake looks speckled

animals.name: Coachwhip
animals.tell: Very long and thin: black at the head, fading to tan at the tail, with scales like a braided whip.
animals.dan: Coachwhip. Long and skinny, five or six feet of snake. Black at the head and tan toward the tail, and his scales look braided like a bullwhip. Not venomous, but he’s fast, and he’d rather be left alone.
animals.draw: an eastern coachwhip (Masticophis flagellum) stretched across sandy scrub, head raised: a very long, slender snake that is black on the head and front third, fading gradually to light tan on the rear half and tail, with large scales on the tail that look like a braided whip, and large eyes

animals.name: Spectacled caiman
animals.tell: A small gator look-alike with a bony ridge between its eyes, like the bridge of a pair of glasses.
animals.dan: Spectacled caiman. Looks like a half-grown gator. But see that ridge between his eyes, like a pair of eyeglasses? He’s from South America. Somebody’s pet, turned loose in the canals around Miami.
animals.draw: a spectacled caiman (Caiman crocodilus) in side view on a canal bank, head to the left: a small crocodilian, olive-brown with dark crossbands on the tail, a moderately broad snout, and a distinct curved bony ridge across the snout between the front of the eyes like the bridge of a pair of spectacles

animals.name: Brown anole
animals.tell: A small brown lizard with a pattern down its back and an orange-red throat fan edged in yellow.
animals.dan: Brown anole. The little brown lizard doing push-ups on every sidewalk in Florida. He came over from Cuba and pushed our green ones up into the treetops.
animals.draw: a brown anole (Anolis sagrei) on a concrete wall edge in side view: a small brown lizard with a pale pattern of chevrons and a light stripe down the back, a short snout, and an extended orange-red throat fan (dewlap) with a yellow edge

animals.name: Tegu
animals.tell: A big, heavy lizard beaded in black and white bands, with a thick tail and a forked tongue.
animals.dan: Tegu. Black and white, long as your arm and then some, flicking a forked tongue. Another pet that got loose. He digs up alligator nests and turtle nests and eats the eggs, so nobody’s glad to see him.
animals.draw: an Argentine black and white tegu (Salvator merianae) walking in side view, head to the left: a large, heavy-bodied lizard with beaded skin in bold black and white bands and spots, a thick muscular tail, strong legs, a pointed head and a pink forked tongue flicking out

animals.name: Glass lizard
animals.tell: It looks like a shiny tan snake with dark stripes, but it blinks: a lizard with no legs at all.
animals.dan: Glass lizard. Now this one’s a trick question. No legs. Slides like a snake. But he’s a lizard. How do you know? He blinks. A snake can’t. And if something grabs him, his tail snaps off like glass.
animals.draw: an eastern glass lizard (Ophisaurus ventralis) on grass: a long, legless, very shiny lizard that looks like a snake, tan-brown with dark stripes along the sides and a greenish tint, a groove along each side of the body, and a lizard-like head with visible eyelids and an ear opening

animals.name: Blue-tailed skink
animals.tell: A small, shiny, striped lizard. The young ones have a tail of bright electric blue.
animals.dan: Skink. Shiny as if somebody waxed him, with stripes down his back, and when he’s young, a bright blue tail. Something grabs that tail, it breaks off and keeps wiggling while he gets away. Then he grows a new one.
animals.draw: a young southeastern five-lined skink (Plestiodon inexpectatus) on a log in side view: a small, sleek, very glossy black lizard with five narrow cream-yellow stripes running from head to tail, and a brilliant electric blue tail

animals.name: House gecko
animals.tell: A pale, bumpy little lizard with big eyes and sticky toes, on the wall by the porch light at night.
animals.dan: House gecko. Pale little fellow with sticky toes, hanging upside down by the porch light after dark, eating moths. He can walk straight across the ceiling. Wish I could.
animals.draw: a Mediterranean house gecko (Hemidactylus turcicus) clinging to a pale stucco wall, seen from above: a small, pale pinkish-tan lizard with bumpy skin and darker mottling, large lidless eyes with vertical pupils, and wide, flattened sticky toe pads on all four feet

animals.name: Snapping turtle
animals.tell: A rough-shelled turtle with a big head, a hooked beak and a long tail with saw teeth along the top.
animals.dan: Snapping turtle. Big head, hooked beak, and a long tail with a saw-tooth ridge like a dinosaur’s. He can’t pull all the way into his shell, so he bites instead. Fast. Don’t test him.
animals.draw: a Florida snapping turtle (Chelydra serpentina osceola) on a muddy bank in side view, head to the left: a freshwater turtle with a rough dark brown shell, a large head with a hooked beak, a thick neck with pointed bumps, heavy clawed legs, and a long thick tail with a saw-toothed ridge along the top

animals.name: Alligator snapping turtle
animals.tell: A giant river turtle with three rows of tall spikes down its shell and a head the size of a football.
animals.dan: Alligator snapping turtle. Three rows of spikes down his back, like something out of a monster movie. He lies on the river bottom with his mouth open, wiggling a little pink bit of his tongue like a worm. Fish comes in for the worm. Snap.
animals.draw: an alligator snapping turtle (Macrochelys temminckii) on a river bottom in side view with its mouth open, head to the left: a huge, prehistoric-looking dark brown turtle with three rows of tall, pointed, spike-like ridges running down its shell, an enormous head with a strongly hooked beak, and a small pink worm-like lure visible on the tongue inside the open mouth

animals.name: Box turtle
animals.tell: A small land turtle with a high dark dome streaked in yellow, able to shut itself in completely.
animals.dan: Box turtle. Little land turtle with yellow streaks on a high dark dome. His shell has a hinge on the bottom. Scare him and he closes up like a box, front door and back.
animals.draw: a Florida box turtle (Terrapene bauri) walking on leaf litter in side view, head to the left: a small land turtle with a high, domed dark brown-black shell marked with bright yellow radiating streaks, and two yellow stripes on the side of the head

animals.name: Leatherback sea turtle
animals.tell: The biggest turtle on earth: no hard shell, just dark leathery skin with long ridges down its back.
animals.dan: Leatherback. Biggest turtle in the world. Heavier than a horse. No hard shell at all, just black leathery skin with ridges running down it. And all that turtle lives on jellyfish.
animals.draw: a leatherback sea turtle (Dermochelys coriacea) swimming in side view, head to the left: an enormous sea turtle with no hard scaly shell, covered instead in smooth dark blue-black leathery skin with white spots and seven long raised ridges running lengthwise down its back, and very long front flippers

animals.name: Green treefrog
animals.tell: A small, smooth, bright green frog with a white stripe down each side and sticky toe pads.
animals.dan: Green treefrog. Bright green with a white racing stripe. He sticks to the window on a rainy night and hollers quonk, quonk, quonk, till the whole neighborhood is up.
animals.draw: a green treefrog (Dryophytes cinereus) clinging to a cattail stem in side view: a small, slender, smooth-skinned bright green frog with a clean white stripe running along each side from the lip to the hind leg, a few tiny gold spots, and round sticky toe pads

animals.name: Cuban treefrog
animals.tell: A big, warty, bug-eyed treefrog with huge toe pads, pale tan or gray.
animals.dan: Cuban treefrog. Twice the size of our green one, warty, with big bug eyes and toe pads like suction cups. He rode in on cargo ships, and he eats our native frogs. His skin slime stings your eyes, so don’t pick him up.
animals.draw: a Cuban treefrog (Osteopilus septentrionalis) clinging to a window frame in side view: a large, stocky treefrog with rough, warty pale tan-gray skin with faint darker blotches, very large bulging eyes, and very large round toe pads

animals.name: Cane toad
animals.tell: A toad as big as a softball, with a large swollen lump behind each eye.
animals.dan: Cane toad. Big as a softball. See the fat lumps behind his eyes? Those ooze a white poison that can kill a dog. Never touch one, and keep your pup well away.
animals.draw: a cane toad (Rhinella marina) sitting on a patio in side view: a very large, heavy, warty tan-brown toad with a pale belly, bony ridges over the eyes, and a large, swollen, triangular gland behind each eye angling down onto the shoulder

animals.name: Pig frog
animals.tell: A big green-brown frog of the marsh, with a pointed nose and fully webbed back feet, that grunts like a pig.
animals.dan: Pig frog. Big green frog out in the sawgrass. You’ll know him by ear. He doesn’t ribbit. He grunts, just like a hog. A whole marsh of them at night sounds like a barnyard.
animals.draw: a pig frog (Lithobates grylio) sitting on a lily pad in side view: a large olive-green to brown frog with scattered dark spots, a rather pointed snout, a large round eardrum behind the eye, and big hind feet webbed all the way to the tips of the toes

animals.name: Brown pelican
animals.tell: A big gray-brown bird with a huge pouch under its bill that dives headfirst from the air.
animals.dan: Brown pelican. Big pouch under the bill, and he dives headfirst like he fell off a roof. We’ve got two regulars out back of my place, Bertha and Oscar.
animals.book: Bertha and Oscar, the pelicans behind Dan’s house.
animals.draw: a brown pelican (Pelecanus occidentalis) standing on a dock piling in side view: a large gray-brown seabird with a very long bill and a big throat pouch, a white and pale yellow head, a chestnut-brown back of the neck, and webbed feet

animals.name: White pelican
animals.tell: A bright white giant with an orange bill and black wingtips that scoops fish while swimming.
animals.dan: White pelican. A good bit bigger than the brown one, bright white, orange bill. He doesn’t dive. He paddles along with his friends and scoops. Comes down for the winter, like half of Ohio.
animals.draw: an American white pelican (Pelecanus erythrorhynchos) floating on calm water in side view: a very large, bright white pelican with a long orange bill and pouch, orange legs, and black flight feathers showing at the wingtip

animals.name: Great blue heron
animals.tell: A tall blue-gray wader with a dagger bill and a black plume over its eye.
animals.dan: Great blue heron. Tall as a fourth-grader, blue-gray, with a bill like a dagger. He stands still as a fence post. If he’s standing where you’re headed, it’s too shallow.
animals.draw: a great blue heron (Ardea herodias) standing in shallow water in side view: a very tall blue-gray wading bird with a long S-curved neck, a long yellow dagger-like bill, a white face with a black plume stripe over the eye, and long dark legs

animals.name: Great egret
animals.tell: A tall all-white wader with a yellow bill and black legs.
animals.dan: Great egret. Tall, all white, yellow bill, black legs. An egret is a white heron, more or less. Remember him by the yellow bill.
animals.draw: a great egret (Ardea alba) standing in shallow water in side view: a tall, slender, entirely white wading bird with a long S-curved neck, a long yellow bill, and long all-black legs and feet

animals.name: Snowy egret
animals.tell: A smaller white wader with a black bill, black legs and bright yellow feet.
animals.dan: Snowy egret. Smaller than the great egret, with a black bill and black legs, and then bright yellow feet. Looks like he’s wearing golden slippers.
animals.draw: a snowy egret (Egretta thula) wading in shallow water in side view, one foot lifted: a small, slender all-white heron with a thin black bill, yellow skin in front of the eye, black legs and conspicuous bright yellow feet

more.cap: The golden slippers: black legs, bright yellow feet.
more.draw: a close-up of the lower legs and feet of a snowy egret standing on wet sand: slender black legs ending in conspicuous bright yellow feet and toes, with the white belly feathers just visible at the top

animals.name: White ibis
animals.tell: A white bird with a long pink-red bill that curves downward, and red legs.
animals.dan: White ibis. White bird with a long red bill curved down like a hook, for poking in the mud. They walk across lawns in a line, like they’re looking for a lost contact lens.
animals.draw: a white ibis (Eudocimus albus) walking in side view: a medium-sized all-white wading bird with a long, slender, strongly down-curved pinkish-red bill, a bare pinkish-red face, and pinkish-red legs

animals.name: Wood stork
animals.tell: A big white wader with a bald, dark, scaly head and a thick bill that droops at the tip.
animals.dan: Wood stork. Big white bird with a bald, wrinkly gray head. Not a handsome fellow. Old-timers call him flinthead. He fishes by feel, with his bill open in the water.
animals.draw: a wood stork (Mycteria americana) standing in shallow water in side view: a large white wading bird with a bald, dark gray, scaly head and neck, a long, thick, slightly down-curved dark bill, long dark legs with pinkish feet, and black on the tail and wing edge

animals.name: Roseate spoonbill
animals.tell: A pink wader with a flat bill shaped like a spoon.
animals.dan: Roseate spoonbill. Pink bird, and half the tourists yell flamingo. Look at the bill. It’s flat and round on the end like a wooden spoon, and he swings it side to side.
animals.draw: a roseate spoonbill (Platalea ajaja) wading in shallow water in side view: a pink wading bird with deeper rose-red shoulders, a white neck, a bald greenish head, red legs, and a long flat bill that widens into a round spoon shape at the tip

more.draw: a close-up of the head of a roseate spoonbill seen from the front and slightly to the side: a bald greenish head, red eye, pink neck, and a long flat gray bill that widens at the tip into a broad, round, flat spoon shape

animals.name: Flamingo
animals.tell: Taller and pinker than a spoonbill, with a very long neck and a thick bill bent in the middle.
animals.dan: Flamingo. The real thing: taller, pinker, with a neck like a garden hose and a bill bent in the middle with a black tip. They’re rare in the wild here, so when you see one, tell everybody.
animals.draw: an American flamingo (Phoenicopterus ruber) standing in shallow water in side view: a very tall, deep coral-pink wading bird with an extremely long thin neck, very long thin pink legs, and a thick bill sharply bent downward in the middle, pale at the base with a black tip

animals.name: Osprey
animals.tell: Brown above, white below, with a white head and a dark stripe through the eye: a hawk that dives feet first for fish.
animals.dan: Osprey. The fish hawk. White head with a dark mask through the eye, white belly. He hovers, folds up, and hits the water feet first. Best fisherman in Florida, and he knows it.
animals.draw: an osprey (Pandion haliaetus) perched on a dead branch holding a fish in its talons, side view: a large hawk, dark brown above and clean white below, with a white head crossed by a bold dark brown stripe through the yellow eye, and a hooked black bill

animals.name: Bald eagle
animals.tell: A huge dark brown bird with a pure white head, a white tail and a big yellow beak.
animals.dan: Bald eagle. Dark brown body, white head, white tail, big yellow beak. Bigger than the osprey, and not above stealing the osprey’s fish right out of the air.
animals.draw: an adult bald eagle (Haliaeetus leucocephalus) perched on a pine branch in side view: a very large raptor with a dark brown body and wings, a pure white head, a pure white tail, a large hooked yellow beak, yellow eyes and yellow feet

animals.name: Red-shouldered hawk
animals.tell: A medium hawk with a rusty-orange barred chest and a black tail with thin white bands.
animals.dan: Red-shouldered hawk. Rusty chest, black-and-white striped tail, and the loudest voice in the swamp. He sits on a wire and screams his own name. Kee-yer, kee-yer.
animals.draw: a red-shouldered hawk (Buteo lineatus) perched on a fence post in side view: a medium-sized hawk with rusty-orange barring on the chest and belly, rusty shoulder patches, brown-and-white checkered wings, and a black tail crossed by narrow white bands

animals.name: Peregrine falcon
animals.tell: Slate-gray, with long pointed wings and a dark helmet and mustache mark on its face.
animals.dan: Peregrine falcon. Pointed wings, gray back, and a dark helmet with a mustache. When he dives on a bird, he’s the fastest animal on earth. Faster than a race car.
animals.draw: a peregrine falcon (Falco peregrinus) perched on a rock ledge in side view: a compact, powerful falcon with a slate blue-gray back, long pointed wings, a pale chest with fine dark bars, and a dark hooded head with a bold dark mustache mark below the eye, yellow eye ring and feet

animals.name: Anhinga
animals.tell: A dark water bird with a snaky neck and a straight, sharp bill, drying its wings spread wide.
animals.dan: Anhinga. Snakebird. He swims with just that long neck sticking out, and spears fish on a bill straight as a needle. Then he hangs his wings out to dry like laundry.
animals.draw: an anhinga (Anhinga anhinga) perched on a branch with wings spread wide to dry, side view: a slender black water bird with silvery-white streaks on the wings, a very long thin snake-like neck, a long, straight, sharply pointed yellow bill, and a long fan-shaped tail

more.cap: A bill straight and sharp as a needle.
more.draw: a close-up of the head and long thin neck of an anhinga in side view: a long, straight, sharply pointed yellow bill like a dagger with no hook at the tip, a small head, a red eye and a snake-like neck

animals.name: Cormorant
animals.tell: A dark water bird with a bill hooked at the tip and an orange patch on its throat.
animals.dan: Cormorant. Looks like an anhinga until you check the bill. His is hooked on the end, and he’s got an orange patch on the throat. They line up on channel markers like they’re waiting for a bus.
animals.draw: a double-crested cormorant (Nannopterum auritum) perched on a channel-marker piling in side view: a stocky black water bird with a thick neck, a bill clearly hooked at the tip, a patch of bare orange-yellow skin on the throat, a bright aqua eye and a short tail

more.cap: A bill hooked at the tip, and an orange throat.
more.draw: a close-up of the head and neck of a double-crested cormorant in side view: a thicker gray bill with a distinct downward hook at the tip, bare orange-yellow skin on the face and throat, and a bright aqua-green eye

animals.name: Frigatebird
animals.tell: A huge black bird soaring on long, narrow, bent wings with a deeply forked tail.
animals.dan: Frigatebird. Man-o’-war bird. Long skinny wings bent like a boomerang, and a tail forked like scissors. He can stay up for days, and he almost never lands on the water. Fishermen follow him to find fish.
animals.draw: a magnificent frigatebird (Fregata magnificens) soaring, seen from below and the side: a very large, all-black seabird with extremely long, narrow, sharply angled wings, a long deeply forked scissor-like tail, a long hooked bill and a small red throat pouch

animals.name: Black skimmer
animals.tell: Black on top, white below, with a red-and-black bill whose bottom half is longer than the top.
animals.dan: Black skimmer. Look at that bill: red and black, and the bottom half is longer than the top. He flies along with it slicing the water, and snaps shut on whatever he bumps.
animals.draw: a black skimmer (Rynchops niger) flying low over calm water in side view with the tip of its lower bill slicing the surface: a long-winged seabird, black above and white below, with a large red-and-black bill whose lower half is clearly longer than the upper, and short red legs

more.cap: The bottom half of the bill is longer than the top.
more.draw: a close-up of the head of a black skimmer in side view: black cap and white face, and a large bill that is red at the base and black at the tip, with the lower half clearly much longer than the upper half

animals.name: Sandhill crane
animals.tell: A tall gray bird with a red cap on its forehead, walking fields and yards in pairs.
animals.dan: Sandhill crane. Tall, gray, with a red cap on his forehead. You’ll see a pair strolling a golf course like they own it. And that rattling bugle call carries a mile.
animals.draw: a sandhill crane (Antigone canadensis) walking in a grassy field in side view: a very tall gray bird with a long neck held straight, a patch of bare red skin on the forehead and crown, white cheeks, a straight dark bill, long black legs and a bustle of drooping feathers over the tail

animals.name: Turkey vulture
animals.tell: A big dark soaring bird with a small bald red head, wings held up in a V, wobbling as it glides.
animals.dan: Turkey vulture. Buzzard, we say. Little bald red head, and he holds his wings up in a V and wobbles like he’s had too much coffee. He’s the cleanup crew. Be grateful.
animals.draw: a turkey vulture (Cathartes aura) perched on a fence post with wings partly open, side view: a large blackish-brown bird with a small, bald, wrinkled red head, a pale hooked bill, and long broad wings that are two-toned dark and silvery-gray underneath

animals.name: Barred owl
animals.tell: A round-headed brown-and-white owl with dark eyes and no ear tufts.
animals.dan: Barred owl. Round head, no ears showing, big dark eyes. You’ll hear him before you see him. He’s the one asking: who cooks for you? Who cooks for you-all?
animals.draw: a barred owl (Strix varia) perched on a cypress branch facing the viewer: a stocky brown-and-white owl with a large round head and no ear tufts, big dark brown eyes, a yellow bill, horizontal bars across the upper chest and vertical streaks down the belly

animals.name: Laughing gull
