animals.tell: A gray-and-white gull that wears a black hood in summer and calls like it’s laughing at you.
animals.dan: Laughing gull. Gray wings, white belly, and in summer a black hood. Sounds exactly like he’s laughing at your casting. Guard your sandwich.
animals.draw: a laughing gull (Leucophaeus atricilla) in summer plumage standing on a beach in side view: a medium-sized gull with a black hood over the head, thin white crescents around the eye, a dark red bill, a white neck and belly, dark gray back and wings with black wingtips, and dark legs

animals.name: Kingfisher
animals.tell: A stocky blue-gray bird with a shaggy crest, a big bill and a white collar.
animals.dan: Kingfisher. Blue-gray, with a shaggy crest like he just woke up, and a bill too big for his body. He hovers over the creek, then dives. Makes a rattle like a broken reel.
animals.draw: a belted kingfisher (Megaceryle alcyon) perched on a branch over a creek in side view: a stocky blue-gray bird with a large head, a shaggy ragged crest, a long thick dagger-like bill, a white collar around the neck, a blue-gray band across a white chest, and tiny feet

animals.name: Great horned owl
animals.tell: A big owl with two feather tufts like horns and round yellow eyes.
animals.dan: Great horned owl. Two feather tufts like horns, and big yellow eyes. Our barred owl has dark eyes and no horns. This one is the boss of the night woods. Even the hawks stay out of his way.
animals.draw: a great horned owl (Bubo virginianus) perched on a pine branch facing the viewer: a large, heavy brown-mottled owl with two prominent feather ear tufts like horns, large round yellow eyes, a rusty-orange face outlined in black, a white throat patch and fine horizontal bars on the belly

animals.name: Burrowing owl
animals.tell: A small owl on long legs that stands beside a hole in the ground in broad daylight.
animals.dan: Burrowing owl. Pint-sized owl on long skinny legs, standing by a hole in the ground in the middle of the day like he’s guarding it. Which he is. That’s his front door.
animals.draw: a burrowing owl (Athene cunicularia) standing upright on sandy ground beside the entrance of a burrow: a small, round-headed brown owl with white spots, no ear tufts, bright yellow eyes with white eyebrows, a barred pale belly, and conspicuously long, bare legs

animals.name: Wild turkey
animals.tell: A big bronze ground bird with a bare red-and-blue head and a tail it spreads like a fan.
animals.dan: Wild turkey. Big bronze bird with a bare red and blue head. The gobbler fans out his tail and struts like he owns the woods. Don’t let the walk fool you. He can fly up into a tree faster than you’d think.
animals.draw: a male wild turkey, Osceola subspecies (Meleagris gallopavo osceola) strutting in side view with its tail fanned: a very large, dark bronze-iridescent ground bird with a bare, wrinkled blue and red head and neck, a red wattle, a hair-like beard hanging from the chest, dark wings with narrow white bars, and a broad fan-shaped tail

animals.name: Mockingbird
animals.tell: A slim gray bird with a long tail and white patches that flash in its wings.
animals.dan: Mockingbird. Florida’s state bird. Slim, gray, with white patches that flash when he flies. He sings every other bird’s song, plus the car alarm, usually at three in the morning.
animals.draw: a northern mockingbird (Mimus polyglottos) perched on a fence post in side view with one wing partly raised: a slim, pale gray songbird with a paler whitish belly, a long dark tail with white outer feathers, dark wings with two white bars and a large white patch, and a thin dark bill

animals.name: Cardinal
animals.tell: Bright red all over, with a pointed crest, a black mask and a thick orange bill.
animals.dan: Cardinal. Redbird. Red from his pointed cap to his tail, with a black mask and a fat orange bill for cracking seeds. The lady is tan with a little red trim. They’re nearly always together.
animals.draw: a male northern cardinal (Cardinalis cardinalis) perched on a branch in side view: a songbird that is brilliant red all over, with a tall pointed crest, a black mask around the eyes and chin, and a short, thick, cone-shaped orange-red bill

animals.name: Pileated woodpecker
animals.tell: A crow-sized black woodpecker with a flaming red crest and a white stripe down its neck.
animals.dan: Pileated woodpecker. Big as a crow, black, with a red crest like a flame. He hammers holes in a dead tree big enough to put your fist in. You’ll hear him a quarter mile off.
animals.draw: a pileated woodpecker (Dryocopus pileatus) clinging upright to a tree trunk in side view: a crow-sized black woodpecker with a tall, pointed flaming red crest, a white stripe running from the bill down the side of the neck, a white chin, and a long chisel-like gray bill

animals.name: Hummingbird
animals.tell: No bigger than your thumb, shiny green, hovering at a flower with its wings a blur.
animals.dan: Hummingbird. No bigger than your thumb. Shiny green back, and the male has a throat like a ruby. He hovers at a flower with his wings going so fast they hum. Weighs about as much as a penny.
animals.draw: a male ruby-throated hummingbird (Archilochus colubris) hovering at a red tubular flower in side view: a tiny bird with a metallic emerald-green back and crown, a brilliant ruby-red throat, a white chest, a long needle-thin black bill, and blurred wings

animals.name: Swallow-tailed kite
animals.tell: Black and white, with long pointed wings and a tail forked deep like scissors, soaring over the swamp.
animals.dan: Swallow-tailed kite. Prettiest bird in the sky, and I’ll argue with anybody. White head, black wings, and a tail forked like scissors. He hardly ever flaps. He just tips that tail and slides across the swamp.
animals.draw: a swallow-tailed kite (Elanoides forficatus) soaring, seen from below and the side: a slim, graceful raptor with a pure white head and underparts, long narrow pointed black wings with white linings, and a very long, deeply forked black scissor-like tail

animals.name: Caracara
animals.tell: A long-legged hawk with a black cap, a white neck and a bare orange face, walking on the ground.
animals.dan: Caracara. Black cap, white neck, orange face, long yellow legs. He’s a falcon that would rather walk than fly. You’ll see him strolling a cow pasture, looking for something the buzzards missed.
animals.draw: a crested caracara (Caracara plancus) standing on a fence post in side view: a large, long-legged raptor with a black cap and shaggy crest, a white neck and cheeks, bare orange-red skin on the face, a pale blue-gray hooked bill, a dark brown-black body, finely barred chest, and long yellow legs

animals.name: Purple gallinule
animals.tell: Purple, blue and green like a jewel, with a red-and-yellow bill and huge yellow feet for walking on lily pads.
animals.dan: Purple gallinule. Looks like somebody painted him: purple, blue and green, red bill with a yellow tip. And look at those feet. Long yellow toes, so he can walk right across the lily pads.
animals.draw: a purple gallinule (Porphyrio martinica) walking across lily pads in side view: a chicken-sized marsh bird with a brilliant purple-blue head, neck and belly, a glossy green back, a pale blue shield on the forehead, a red bill with a yellow tip, and very long yellow legs and toes

animals.name: Florida scrub-jay
animals.tell: A blue-and-gray jay with no crest, found in Florida scrub and nowhere else in the world.
animals.dan: Florida scrub-jay. Blue head, blue wings, gray back, no crest. Now listen. This bird lives in Florida and no place else on the whole earth. And he’s so curious he’ll come right up to look at you. Don’t feed him. Just look back.
animals.draw: a Florida scrub-jay (Aphelocoma coerulescens) perched on top of a scrub oak in side view: a slim jay with a blue head, wings and long tail, a pale gray back and belly, a whitish forehead and throat with a faint blue-gray necklace, NO crest, and a stout black bill

animals.name: Oystercatcher
animals.tell: A black-and-white shorebird with a long, bright orange bill like a carrot.
animals.dan: Oystercatcher. Black head, white belly, and a long orange bill like a carrot. He uses it like a knife, to pry open oysters. Which is more than I can do without cutting my thumb.
animals.draw: an American oystercatcher (Haematopus palliatus) standing on an oyster bar in side view: a stocky shorebird with a black head and neck, a dark brown back, a white belly, a long, straight, bright orange-red bill, a yellow eye with a red ring, and pale pink legs

animals.name: Black vulture
animals.tell: A black soaring bird with a bald gray head, a short tail and white patches at the tips of its wings.
animals.dan: Black vulture. The other buzzard. Gray wrinkly head where the turkey vulture’s is red, a short stubby tail, and white patches out at his wingtips. He flaps a lot more, too.
animals.draw: a black vulture (Coragyps atratus) standing on a fence post with wings partly spread, side view: a large all-black bird with a bald, wrinkled dark gray head and neck, a short squared tail, a thin dark bill with a pale tip, and whitish patches at the tips of the wings

animals.name: Green heron
animals.tell: A small, hunched heron with a chestnut neck and a dark green cap, crouched at the water’s edge.
animals.dan: Green heron. Little hunched-up heron, chestnut neck, dark green cap. Smartest fisherman on the creek. He’ll drop a bug on the water for bait and wait for a minnow to come up. I’m not making that up.
animals.draw: a green heron (Butorides virescens) crouched on a mangrove root at the water’s edge in side view: a small, stocky, short-legged heron with a dark glossy green-black cap and back, a rich chestnut neck and chest, a dagger-like dark bill, and yellow-orange legs

animals.name: Manatee
animals.tell: A big, slow, gray animal with a whiskered snout and a round paddle for a tail.
animals.dan: Manatee. Sea cow. Big, gray, slow and gentle, with a tail like a paddle. Mostly you’ll see a nose come up to breathe. Slow the boat right down. Look, don’t touch.
animals.draw: a West Indian manatee (Trichechus manatus) swimming in clear shallow water in side view: a very large, plump, wrinkled gray mammal with a whiskered, blunt square snout, small eyes, two front flippers with nails, no dorsal fin, and a broad, flat, rounded paddle-shaped tail

animals.name: Bottlenose dolphin
animals.tell: Sleek and gray with a curved back fin, a short beak, and a tail that beats up and down.
animals.dan: Bottlenose dolphin. See a fin and can’t tell? Watch the tail. A dolphin’s tail beats up and down, so his back rolls over the top. A shark’s tail sweeps side to side.
animals.book: The playful pair at Lopez River.
animals.draw: a bottlenose dolphin (Tursiops truncatus) leaping in side view: a sleek, muscular gray marine mammal with a paler belly, a short rounded beak with a smiling mouth line, a curved (falcate) dorsal fin, and horizontal tail flukes

more.cap: At the surface. Left, a dolphin: one curved fin and a rolling back. Right, a shark: two points, the fin and the tip of the tail.
more.draw: two animals at the calm surface of the sea seen from the side, clearly separated left and right. On the LEFT a bottlenose dolphin surfacing: a curved, backward-hooked dorsal fin on a smooth, rounded gray back that arches out of the water. On the RIGHT a shark cruising at the surface: a taller, straighter triangular dorsal fin, and a short distance behind it the pointed tip of the upright tail fin also cutting the surface, with no back showing

animals.name: Florida panther
animals.tell: A big, plain tan cat with a long tail tipped in black.
animals.dan: Florida panther. Big tan cat, no spots, with a long, heavy rope of a tail. There are only a couple hundred left in the whole world, and they all live here. Most Floridians never see one.
animals.draw: a Florida panther (Puma concolor coryi) walking through sawgrass and palmetto in side view: a large, lean, plain tawny-tan cat with no spots, a pale muzzle and chest, small rounded ears, and a very long thick tail with a black tip

animals.name: Bobcat
animals.tell: A spotted cat twice the size of a house cat, with a short stubby tail and tufted ears.
animals.dan: Bobcat. Twice the size of a house cat, spotted, with a stub of a tail. That’s the tell: short tail, bobcat. Long tail, panther.
animals.draw: a bobcat (Lynx rufus) standing on a fallen log in side view: a medium-sized tan cat about twice the size of a house cat, with dark spots and bars on its coat, a ruff of fur on the cheeks, black tufts on the ear tips, long legs and a very short stubby bobbed tail with a black tip

animals.name: Black bear
animals.tell: Florida’s only bear: glossy black, with a tan muzzle and round ears.
animals.dan: Black bear. The only bear we’ve got. Black coat, tan muzzle. He’d rather have your garbage than have anything to do with you. Give him the whole road.
animals.draw: a Florida black bear (Ursus americanus floridanus) walking through pine flatwoods in side view: a stocky bear with a glossy black coat, a tan-brown muzzle, small round ears, and a small pale patch on the chest

animals.name: River otter
animals.tell: Long, sleek and brown, with a thick tail that tapers to a point and a whiskery face.
animals.dan: River otter. Long, sleek and brown, with whiskers and a thick tail. He’ll pop up by the boat, give you a look, and go right back to playing. Happiest animal in the swamp.
animals.draw: a North American river otter (Lontra canadensis) on a river bank, half out of the water, in side view: a long, sleek, dark brown mammal with a paler throat, a broad whiskered face, small ears, webbed feet, and a long, thick tail that tapers to a point

animals.name: Raccoon
animals.tell: A black mask across the eyes and a bushy tail with dark rings.
animals.dan: Raccoon. Black mask, ringed tail, and hands like a burglar. He’ll open your cooler, eat your bait, and wash his hands after. Latch everything.
animals.draw: a raccoon (Procyon lotor) standing at the water’s edge among mangrove roots in side view: a stocky gray-brown mammal with a black mask across the eyes outlined in white, a pointed snout, hand-like front paws, and a bushy tail with dark rings

animals.name: Key deer
animals.tell: A deer no bigger than a large dog, living only in the Florida Keys.
animals.dan: Key deer. A whole deer about the size of a big dog. They live down in the Keys and no place else on earth. They get tame and will walk right up to you. Don’t feed them, and don’t walk up to them.
animals.draw: a Key deer (Odocoileus virginianus clavium) standing among low palms in side view: a very small, dainty white-tailed deer about the size of a large dog, tan-brown with a white belly and throat, large ears, big dark eyes and a small set of antlers

animals.name: Armadillo
animals.tell: Wearing armor: a shell of bony bands, a long snout and a scaly tail.
animals.dan: Armadillo. A possum in a suit of armor. Nine bands across his middle and a long nose for digging up bugs. Scare him, and he jumps straight up in the air.
animals.draw: a nine-banded armadillo (Dasypus novemcinctus) walking on sandy ground in side view: a small gray-brown mammal covered in a bony armored shell with a series of flexible bands across the middle, a long pointed snout, upright mule-like ears, and a long, tapering, ringed scaly tail

animals.name: Opossum
animals.tell: Gray fur, a pointed white face with a pink nose, and a long bare tail like a rat’s.
animals.dan: Possum. White pointy face, pink nose, bare tail. The only animal north of Mexico that carries her babies in a pouch, like a kangaroo. Scare her bad enough, and she falls over and plays dead.
animals.draw: a Virginia opossum (Didelphis virginiana) walking along a fence rail in side view, head to the left: a cat-sized mammal with shaggy gray fur, a long pointed white face with a pink nose and black eyes, thin black ears, and a long, bare, scaly pinkish tail

animals.name: White-tailed deer
animals.tell: A tan deer that flips up a tail white underneath, like a flag, when it runs.
animals.dan: White-tailed deer. Tan coat, and when he runs, up goes the tail, white underneath like a flag. That’s him telling every other deer in the woods there’s trouble.
animals.draw: a white-tailed deer buck (Odocoileus virginianus) bounding away in side view with its tail raised: a slender tan-brown deer with a white belly and throat, a set of forward-curving antlers, and a tail held straight up showing its bright white underside like a flag

animals.name: Wild hog
animals.tell: A dark, bristly pig with a long snout and tusks, rooting up the ground.
animals.dan: Wild hog. Dark, hairy, long snout, tusks. The Spanish turned pigs loose here five hundred years ago, and they never left. A bunch of them will plow up a pasture overnight. Give a big boar plenty of room.
animals.draw: a feral hog (Sus scrofa) rooting in the ground in side view, head to the left: a lean, powerful dark brown-black pig with coarse bristly hair, a ridge of longer bristles along the spine, a long narrow snout, small eyes, upright ears, short curved tusks at the mouth and a straight tail

animals.name: Coyote
animals.tell: A lean gray-tan wild dog with big pointed ears and a bushy tail carried low.
animals.dan: Coyote. Skinny gray-tan dog, big pointed ears, bushy tail hanging low. Coyotes weren’t always in Florida. They walked in on their own, and now they’re in every county. You’ll hear them yipping at night.
animals.draw: a coyote (Canis latrans) trotting in side view, head to the left: a lean, medium-sized wild dog with grizzled gray-tan fur, rusty legs and ears, large upright pointed ears, a narrow pointed muzzle, yellow eyes, and a bushy black-tipped tail carried low

animals.name: Gray fox
animals.tell: A small fox: gray on top, rusty on the sides, with a black stripe down a bushy tail.
animals.dan: Gray fox. Gray on top, rusty on his sides, and a black stripe down his tail. Here’s what makes him special. He’s the only wild dog in North America that climbs trees. Goes right up like a cat.
animals.draw: a gray fox (Urocyon cinereoargenteus) standing on a fallen log in side view, head to the left: a small, cat-sized fox with a grizzled salt-and-pepper gray back, rusty-orange fur on the neck, sides and legs, a white throat, pointed ears, and a long bushy tail with a black stripe along the top and a black tip

animals.name: Marsh rabbit
animals.tell: A small dark brown rabbit with short ears and no white cotton on its tail, at home in the water.
animals.dan: Marsh rabbit. Small, dark brown, short ears. Look at his tail: no white cotton ball. And here’s the strange part. He swims. Something chases him and he jumps in and paddles off like a muskrat.
animals.draw: a marsh rabbit (Sylvilagus palustris) sitting at the edge of marsh grass and water in side view: a small, dark chocolate-brown rabbit with short rounded ears, small feet, dark eyes, and a small dingy gray-brown tail with no white cotton-ball underside

animals.name: Bat
animals.tell: A small brown, furry animal with leathery wings, out at dusk.
animals.dan: Bat. Little brown fellow with leather wings. He comes out at sunset and eats hundreds of bugs a night, so around here he’s a hero. He steers in the dark by listening to his own echo. Never pick one up.
animals.draw: a Brazilian free-tailed bat (Tadarida brasiliensis) in flight seen from the side and slightly below, wings spread: a small bat with dark brown velvety fur, broad forward-pointing ears, narrow leathery dark wings, and a short tail that extends beyond the tail membrane

animals.name: Right whale
animals.tell: A huge black whale with no fin on its back and rough white patches on its head.
animals.dan: Right whale. Longer than a school bus, black, no fin on his back at all, and rough white patches on his head. The mamas come down to the Florida coast every winter to have their calves. There are only a few hundred left in the whole world.
animals.draw: a North Atlantic right whale (Eubalaena glacialis) at the surface in side view, head to the left, with a V-shaped spout: an enormous, stocky black whale with NO dorsal fin, a huge head with rough whitish-gray patches of thickened skin (callosities) on top and along the jaw, a strongly arched mouth line, and broad paddle-shaped flippers

animals.name: Portuguese man-o’-war
animals.tell: A blue-purple balloon floating on top of the water, trailing long blue strings.
animals.dan: Portuguese man-o’-war. Looks like a blue balloon somebody lost. Under it hang stinging strings longer than this boat. Never touch one. Not in the water, and not washed up dead on the beach. They still sting.
animals.draw: a Portuguese man-o’-war (Physalia physalis) floating at the sea surface, seen from the side with the waterline shown: a translucent blue and purple gas-filled float shaped like a balloon with a pink-tinged crest along the top, above the water, and a mass of long, thin, dark blue trailing tentacles hanging down below the surface

animals.name: Moon jellyfish
animals.tell: A clear saucer with four pale pink rings in the middle, drifting.
animals.dan: Moon jelly. A clear saucer with four pink rings, like a four-leaf clover, drifting along. His sting is mild. But you leave him be, and any jellyfish you can’t name, too.
animals.draw: a moon jellyfish (Aurelia aurita) drifting in blue-green water, seen from the side and slightly above: a translucent, pale saucer-shaped bell with a fringe of short fine tentacles around the edge and four pale pink horseshoe-shaped rings visible in the centre like a four-leaf clover

animals.name: Octopus
animals.tell: Eight arms lined with suckers, a soft bag of a body and no bones at all.
animals.dan: Octopus. Eight arms, three hearts, no bones. He can squeeze through a hole the size of a quarter and change color to match the rock he’s sitting on. Smartest thing in the ocean without a backbone.
animals.draw: a common octopus (Octopus vulgaris) on a rocky seabed: a soft-bodied animal with a rounded mottled reddish-brown bag-like body, raised eyes with horizontal pupils, and eight long curling arms lined with two rows of pale suckers

animals.name: Reef squid
animals.tell: A torpedo with fins rippling down both sides, big eyes, and arms bunched out front.
animals.dan: Reef squid. A little torpedo with a fin running down each side and all his arms bunched out front. They hover in a line like airplanes in formation, and flash colors at each other. That’s how they signal.
animals.draw: a Caribbean reef squid (Sepioteuthis sepioidea) hovering in clear water in side view, arms to the left: a torpedo-shaped squid with a mottled brown, green and iridescent body, undulating fins running along almost the full length of each side, very large eyes, and a bunch of short arms held together and pointing forward

animals.name: Sea star
animals.tell: A thick orange star with five short, fat arms and a net of raised knobs on its back.
animals.dan: Sea star. Starfish, most folks say. Fat orange star with five stubby arms, down in the seagrass. If he loses an arm he grows another. Look at him right where he lies. Out of the water, he can’t breathe.
animals.draw: a red cushion sea star (Oreaster reticulatus) on a seagrass bed seen from above: a thick, heavy, inflated orange-red sea star with five short, broad arms and a raised net-like pattern of knobby tubercles across its back

animals.name: Sea urchin
animals.tell: A black ball of long, thin needles, wedged in the rocks.
animals.dan: Sea urchin. A black ball of needles tucked into the rocks. The needles break off in your foot, and they hurt for a week. This is why we wear shoes on the reef, and why we watch where we put our hands.
animals.draw: a long-spined sea urchin (Diadema antillarum) wedged in a crevice of reef rock, seen from the side: a small black ball-shaped body bristling in all directions with very long, thin, sharp black needle-like spines

animals.name: Sand dollar
animals.tell: A flat, round disc with a flower of five petals on top.
animals.dan: Sand dollar. Flat as a cookie, with a five-petal flower on top. The white ones on the beach are empty shells. If he’s brown and fuzzy, he’s alive, so leave him right where he is.
animals.draw: two sand dollars lying side by side on wet sand seen from above: on the left a living five-holed keyhole sand dollar, a flat round disc that is dark brownish-purple and velvety with fine fuzz and five slot-like holes; on the right a dead bleached white one of the same shape showing clearly the five-petalled flower pattern on its top

animals.name: Queen conch
animals.tell: A big, heavy spiral shell with a wide lip that is glossy pink inside.
animals.dan: Queen conch. Say it konk. Big heavy shell, pink as a sunrise inside. The fellow who lives in there peeks out with two eyes on stalks and hops along on one foot. Folks born in the Keys call themselves Conchs, after him.
animals.draw: a queen conch (Aliger gigas) on a sandy seagrass bottom, tilted so the opening shows: a large, heavy spiral sea shell with blunt spines on its shoulders, a wide flared lip that is glossy pink inside, and the living animal partly out, showing two eyes on long stalks

animals.name: Hermit crab
animals.tell: A small crab wearing somebody else’s seashell on its back.
animals.dan: Hermit crab. He’s got no hard shell of his own on his back end, so he moves into an empty snail shell and carries it around. When he outgrows it, he goes house hunting. Never pull one out. He’d sooner come apart.
animals.draw: a land hermit crab (Coenobita clypeatus) walking on sand in side view: a small reddish-purple crab with one large purple claw, stalked eyes and long antennae, its soft rear body hidden inside a borrowed spiral snail shell that it carries on its back

animals.name: Fiddler crab
animals.tell: A crab the size of a quarter with one giant claw, waving it on the mud flat.
animals.dan: Fiddler crab. Size of a quarter. The male has one claw as big as the rest of him, and he waves it around like he’s playing the fiddle. Walk out on a mud flat and a thousand of them duck into their holes at once.
animals.draw: a male sand fiddler crab (Leptuca pugilator) on a mud flat beside its burrow hole, seen from the front and side: a very small squarish tan-and-purple crab with eyes on tall thin stalks, one tiny claw and one enormously oversized pale claw, as large as its body, held raised

animals.name: Ghost crab
animals.tell: A pale, sand-colored crab with a square body and eyes on tall stalks, running sideways on the beach.
animals.dan: Ghost crab. The color of dry sand, eyes up on stalks like periscopes. He runs sideways across the beach at night so fast you’re not sure you saw him. That’s why he’s the ghost.
animals.draw: an Atlantic ghost crab (Ocypode quadrata) running across dry beach sand in side-front view: a pale sandy-white crab with a squarish box-like body, long pale legs, two unequal whitish claws, and large black eyes on tall upright stalks

animals.name: Pink shrimp
animals.tell: See-through pinkish, with long whisker antennae, a fan for a tail, and a dark spot on its side.
animals.dan: Shrimp. See-through pink, long whiskers, a fan for a tail. When he’s scared he snaps that tail and shoots off backwards. Everything in the bay eats him, and that’s why fishermen use him for bait.
animals.draw: a northern pink shrimp (Farfantepenaeus duorarum) swimming in side view, head to the left: a translucent pinkish-tan shrimp with a segmented curved body, a dark reddish-brown spot on the side of the tail section, a toothed spike (rostrum) above the eyes, black stalked eyes, very long thin antennae sweeping back, many small legs, and a fan-shaped tail

animals.name: Seahorse
animals.tell: A tiny fish with a horse’s head, swimming upright, its tail curled round a blade of grass.
animals.dan: Seahorse. A fish with a horse’s head that swims standing up and holds on to the seagrass with his tail. And here’s one for you. It’s the daddy seahorse who carries the babies. In a pouch.
animals.draw: a lined seahorse (Hippocampus erectus) holding a blade of seagrass with its curled tail, in side view facing left: a small upright fish with a horse-like head and tubular snout, a bony ridged brownish-yellow body with fine pale lines on the head and neck, a small fin on its back and a prehensile tail curled around the grass

animals.name: Stone crab
animals.tell: A thick, smooth, brownish crab with oversized claws tipped in black.
animals.dan: Stone crab. Heavy brown shell, and big claws with black tips that can crack an oyster. Best eating in Florida. Keep your fingers out of there.
animals.book: Matt begging claws from the seafood company as a kid.
animals.draw: a Florida stone crab (Menippe mercenaria) seen from the front and above: a stout crab with a thick, smooth, oval brownish-red shell with gray spots, and two very large, heavy claws with distinct black tips

animals.name: Blue crab
animals.tell: An olive shell with a sharp point on each side, bright blue claws and back legs like paddles.
animals.dan: Blue crab. Blue claws, a sharp point on each side of the shell, and back legs shaped like paddles. He swims sideways, fast, and he pinches like he means it.
animals.draw: a blue crab (Callinectes sapidus) seen from above: a crab with a wide olive-green shell drawn out into one long sharp spine on each side, bright blue claws and legs, and the rear pair of legs flattened into paddles for swimming

animals.name: Spiny lobster
animals.tell: A lobster with no big claws: just long whip antennae, a spiny shell and spots on its tail.
animals.dan: Spiny lobster. Florida’s lobster has no big claws at all. Just two long whips for antennae and spines all over. He walks the reef at night, backwards when he’s scared.
animals.draw: a Caribbean spiny lobster (Panulirus argus) seen from the side and above: a lobster with NO large claws, two very long, thick, whip-like spiny antennae, a spiny brown-and-tan shell with forward-pointing horns over the eyes, and a banded tail with large cream spots

animals.name: Horseshoe crab
animals.tell: A smooth brown shell shaped like a helmet, with a long spike of a tail.
animals.dan: Horseshoe crab. A brown helmet with a spike for a tail. Looks scary. Completely harmless. His family has been walking these beaches since before the dinosaurs.
animals.draw: an Atlantic horseshoe crab (Limulus polyphemus) on wet sand seen from above and slightly to the side: a smooth, domed, olive-brown horseshoe-shaped shell like a helmet, a hinged spiny rear section, and a long, straight, pointed spike of a tail

animals.name: Black widow spider
animals.tell: A shiny black spider with a round body and a red hourglass on its underside.
animals.dan: Black widow. Shiny black, round as a marble, with a red hourglass on her belly. She’s venomous, and she likes woodpiles, old buckets and the underside of the dock box. So you look before you reach.
animals.draw: a female southern black widow spider (Latrodectus mactans) hanging upside down in an irregular web so that her underside faces the viewer: a glossy jet-black spider with a large, round, shiny abdomen marked on its underside with a bright red hourglass shape, and long slender black legs

animals.name: Banana spider
animals.tell: A big spider with a long yellow body and fuzzy tufts on its legs, in the middle of a golden web.
animals.dan: Banana spider. Long yellow body, and legs with little fuzzy leg warmers. She’s as big as your hand, and her web shines gold in the sun. She looks like a nightmare, and she just wants to be left alone. Duck under the web.
animals.draw: a female golden silk orb-weaver (Trichonephila clavipes) in the centre of a large golden-yellow web: a large spider with a long, cylindrical yellow-olive abdomen with pale spots, a silvery-white head section, and very long banded brown-and-yellow legs with dark fuzzy tufts of hair at the joints

animals.name: Scorpion
animals.tell: Two pincers out front and a jointed tail curled over its back with a stinger on the tip.
animals.dan: Scorpion. Pincers out front, and a tail curled up over his back with a stinger on the end. Ours is small and brown, and he hides under bark and boards. The sting hurts, about like a wasp’s. Shake out your boots.
animals.draw: a Florida bark scorpion (Centruroides gracilis) on a piece of tree bark seen from above and the side: a slender dark reddish-brown scorpion with two long, thin pincers held forward, eight legs, and a long, thin, segmented tail arched over its back ending in a curved stinger

animals.name: Fire ant
animals.tell: Tiny reddish ants pouring out of a dome of loose dirt that has no hole in the top.
animals.dan: Fire ant. Tiny, reddish, and mean. Their mound is a dome of loose dirt with no hole on top. Step on it and they pour out by the hundreds, climb your leg, and all sting at once. So you watch where you stand.
animals.draw: a red imported fire ant mound in grass with ants swarming over it, and one worker ant shown large and close in the foreground in side view: a low dome of loose, crumbly soil with no opening on top; the ant is small, reddish-brown with a darker rear section, a two-segment waist and bent antennae

animals.name: Lubber grasshopper
animals.tell: A huge yellow-and-black grasshopper, as long as your finger, too heavy to fly and in no hurry.
animals.dan: Lubber grasshopper. Big as your finger, yellow and black with a little red on him. Too heavy to fly and too slow to hop. He doesn’t need to. He tastes so awful that most birds and lizards leave him alone, and those colors are his warning sign.
animals.draw: an eastern lubber grasshopper (Romalea microptera) on a plant stem in side view, head to the left: a very large, heavy-bodied grasshopper, yellow-orange with black markings, short forewings tinged with rose-red that do not reach the end of the abdomen, and thick hind legs

animals.name: Dragonfly
animals.tell: A long thin body, giant eyes, and four clear wings held straight out like an airplane.
animals.dan: Dragonfly. Skeeter hawk. Four clear wings held straight out, eyes that cover his whole head. He catches mosquitoes right out of the air and eats them on the wing. Never hurt a soul. I’m always glad to see him.
animals.draw: a blue dasher dragonfly (Pachydiplax longipennis) perched on the tip of a reed in side view with wings spread: a slender insect with a long powder-blue abdomen with a dark tip, a yellow-striped thorax, huge green compound eyes covering most of the head, and four long, clear, finely veined wings held straight out to the sides

animals.name: Monarch butterfly
animals.tell: Orange wings with black veins like stained glass and a black border dotted in white.
animals.dan: Monarch. Orange wings with black lines like a stained-glass window, and white dots round the edge. Some of them fly all the way to Mexico for the winter, on wings thinner than paper.
animals.draw: a monarch butterfly (Danaus plexippus) perched on a milkweed flower with wings open, seen from above: large bright orange wings with bold black veins and a wide black border dotted with two rows of small white spots, and a black body with white dots

animals.name: Zebra longwing
animals.tell: Long, narrow black wings with yellow stripes, like a zebra’s.
animals.dan: Zebra longwing. Long black wings with yellow stripes. Florida’s state butterfly. He floats along slow, like he’s got nowhere to be. At night a whole bunch of them sleep together on the same branch.
animals.draw: a zebra longwing butterfly (Heliconius charithonia) perched with wings open, seen from above: long, narrow black wings crossed by several bold pale yellow stripes, with a row of small yellow dots along the lower edge of the hindwings, and a slender black body

animals.name: Firefly
animals.tell: A small dark beetle whose tail end blinks yellow-green in the dark.
animals.dan: Firefly. Lightning bug. A little dark beetle with a lantern in his tail. On a summer night the whole edge of the woods blinks on and off. He’s signaling to his sweetheart. Best seen from the porch, with the lights off.
animals.draw: a firefly beetle (Photinus) clinging to a blade of grass at dusk in side view: a small, soft, elongated dark brown beetle with a reddish-pink shield behind the head marked with a dark spot, pale edges on the wing covers, and the last segments of the abdomen glowing bright yellow-green

animals.name: Lovebug
animals.tell: A small black fly with a red-orange patch behind its head, flying stuck to its partner.
animals.dan: Lovebug. Little black fly with an orange spot behind his head, and he’s always stuck to his sweetheart, flying in pairs. Twice a year there are millions of them, and they end up on the front of every car on the highway.
animals.draw: a pair of lovebugs (Plecia nearctica) joined tail to tail on a blade of grass, in side view: two small, slender black flies, each with a red-orange patch on top of the thorax just behind the head and smoky dark wings, attached to each other end to end

animals.name: Mosquito
animals.tell: Thin as a thread, with long legs and a needle for a mouth.
animals.dan: Mosquito. You know this one already. Long legs, a needle for a mouth, and a whine in your ear. Only the females bite. Folks around here joke that she’s the state bird. Long sleeves at sundown, and bring the spray.
animals.draw: a mosquito (Aedes) standing on skin in side view about to bite: a tiny, very slender insect with a dark body with white bands on the legs and abdomen, long thin legs, a long needle-like mouthpart pointing down, feathery antennae and narrow clear wings

animals.name: Cicada
animals.tell: A stout green-and-black bug with bulging eyes and clear wings, buzzing from the treetops.
animals.dan: Cicada. Fat green and black bug with clear wings and eyes set wide apart. That buzz you hear on a hot afternoon, the one that sounds like a power line? That’s him. He leaves his empty brown skin stuck to the tree bark.
animals.draw: a cicada (Neotibicen) clinging to tree bark in side view, with its empty shed brown shell also clinging to the bark just below it: a stout, thick-bodied insect with a black and green patterned body, a broad head with bulging eyes set far apart, and long, clear, veined wings folded like a roof over its back

animals.name: Palmetto bug
animals.tell: A big, flat, reddish-brown roach as long as your thumb, with long feelers. And it flies.
animals.dan: Palmetto bug. That’s the polite Florida word for a giant roach. Reddish brown, long as your thumb, long feelers. And yes, he flies. Usually straight at your face. He doesn’t bite or sting. You’ll holler anyway. Everybody does.
animals.draw: an American cockroach or palmetto bug (Periplaneta americana) on a palmetto frond seen from above: a large, flat, oval, glossy reddish-brown insect with a pale yellowish band on the shield behind the head, long wings covering the abdomen, spiny legs and very long thin antennae
